senses.title: Neither very large nor very small
senses.definition: of a size, amount or level that sits between the extremes
senses.definitionCN: 处在两端之间的大小、数量或水平
senses.example: Hire a car of moderate size for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 租一辆中等大小的车用一周。
senses.why: Latin modus meant a measure, and moderatus described what is kept inside its measure, so the adjective starts from a proper limit rather than from the middle point itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 modus 意为尺度，moderatus 描述的是被保持在尺度之内的东西，所以这个形容词的起点是「有恰当的界限」，而不是「正中间那一点」。

senses.title: Not extreme in opinion
senses.definition: holding views that avoid the extremes, especially in politics or religion
senses.definitionCN: 尤指在政治或宗教上不持极端立场
senses.example: Her moderate views made her acceptable to both camps.
senses.exampleCN: 她温和的立场让两个阵营都能接受她。
senses.why: A person who stays inside measure in argument was called moderate, because the same limit that governs quantity also governs how far an opinion should go.
senses.whyCN: 在争论中守住尺度的人被称为 moderate，因为约束数量的那条界限，也同样约束一种观点可以走多远。

senses.title: To make less intense
senses.definition: to make a feeling, force or rate become less strong or less fast
senses.definitionCN: 使情绪、力量或速度变得不那么强烈或快速
senses.example: The doctor moderated the dose after the fever dropped.
senses.exampleCN: 退烧之后医生把剂量调低了。
senses.why: The verb came from the same participle: to moderate is to put something back inside its measure, which in practice means turning down what has grown too strong.
senses.whyCN: 动词出自同一个分词：to moderate 就是把某样东西重新放回尺度之内，落到实际里就是把长过头的东西压下去。

senses.title: To preside over a discussion
senses.definition: to lead a debate or discussion and keep it orderly and fair
senses.definitionCN: 引导辩论或讨论，使其有序而公正
senses.example: She moderated the panel without letting anyone dominate.
senses.exampleCN: 她主持座谈，没让任何人独占话语。
senses.why: A chair does to a conversation what the adjective does to a quantity: keeps it within limits, so the verb moved from controlling force to controlling talk.
senses.whyCN: 主席对谈话做的事，正如形容词对数量做的事——把它守在界限内；于是动词从控制力量走到了控制发言。

intro.en: Moderate comes from Latin moderatus, the participle of moderari, to keep something within a measure, and that measure is modus.
intro.cn: moderate 出自拉丁语 moderatus，它是 moderari（把某物守在尺度内）的分词，而那条尺度就是 modus。

items.en: Modus meant a measure, a due amount or a manner, and it is the small noun inside a large family of English words about limits and ways.
items.cn: modus 意为尺度、适当的分量、方式，它是英语里一大族关于界限与方式的词所共有的那个小名词。

items.en: Moderari meant to keep within measure, to set a limit or to guide, and it was used of weather, of temper and of people in charge.
items.cn: moderari 意为守在尺度内、设定界限或引导，既用于天气与脾气，也用于掌事的人。

items.en: Its participle moderatus described what had been held inside its measure, and from that participle English took the adjective.
items.cn: 它的分词 moderatus 描述已经被守在尺度内的东西，英语的形容词正是从这个分词来的。

items.en: English borrowed moderate in the fifteenth century as an adjective of quantity and of temper, then formed the verb from it.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 moderate，用作数量与脾气的形容词，随后又由它造出动词。

items.en: Modern English added the public sense of presiding over a debate, where the limit being kept is the order of the discussion rather than the strength of anything.
items.cn: 现代英语加上了主持辩论的公共义，此时被守住的界限是讨论的秩序，而不是某样东西的强度。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin measure word modus through its English family; the near-meaning group gathers words for what stays mild or within bounds.
note.cn: 形近组顺着拉丁语「尺度」modus 及其英语词族展开；近义组收表示温和或守在有界之内的词。

entries.definition: The quality of keeping things within sensible limits.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物守在有分寸的界限内的品质。

entries.definition: A person who chairs a discussion and keeps it orderly.
entries.definitionCN: 主持讨论并维持秩序的人。

entries.definition: Going far beyond a sensible limit.
entries.definitionCN: 远远超出合理限度的。

entries.definition: To a limited but not small degree.
entries.definitionCN: 程度有限但不算小的；适度地。

entries.definition: Not strong or severe in effect.
entries.definitionCN: 作用不强烈、不严重的。

entries.definition: Kept within limits, especially of climate or of appetite.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指气候或欲望被守在限度之内的。

entries.definition: Not large in size or amount; not boastful.
entries.definitionCN: 规模或数量不大的；不自夸的。

entries.definition: Held back from going too far.
entries.definitionCN: 被克制住、不走得太远的。

normalIntro.en: A Latin word for measure runs through this family, so every member is about staying inside a line rather than about being weak.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁语的「尺度」贯穿这个词族，所以每个成员说的都是「守在一条线内」，而不是「软弱」。

normal.en: Modus, the Latin word for measure, sits inside moderate, moderation and immoderate, so all three talk about limits.
normal.cn: modus 是拉丁语「尺度」，它藏在 moderate、moderation 与 immoderate 里，所以这三个词说的都是界限。

normal.en: Moderari is the verb of keeping within measure, and the adjective moderatus plus English moderate are its direct descendants.
normal.cn: moderari 是「守在尺度内」的动词，形容词 moderatus 与英语 moderate 都是它的直系后代。

normal.en: Adding -ly gives moderately, -ion gives moderation, -or gives the person who keeps order, so one stem makes adverb, noun and person.
normal.cn: 加 -ly 得 moderately，加 -ion 得 moderation，加 -or 得那个维持秩序的人，一个词干造出副词、名词和人。

normal.en: Im- before moderate reverses it, so immoderate is exactly what has escaped its measure.
normal.cn: im- 加在 moderate 前面把意思反转，于是 immoderate 正是「跑出尺度之外」的东西。

normal.en: The debate sense shows the metaphor at work: a chair keeps the talk inside bounds, as a doctor keeps a dose inside bounds.
normal.cn: 辩论义把这个比喻摆了出来：主席把发言守在范围内，正如医生把剂量守在范围内。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing down on a flame that has grown too high, lowering it without putting it out.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按住蹿得过高的火苗，把它压低却不弄灭。

abstract.en: A single word covers a medium size, a calm opinion and a chaired debate, because all three are about staying inside a line.
abstract.cn: 同一个词涵盖了中等尺寸、平和的立场和被主持的辩论，因为三者都在讲「守在一条线内」。

abstract.en: Moderation is not the absence of force but its measured release, which is why the same verb can calm a fever and steer a panel.
abstract.cn: 节制不是没有力量，而是有分寸地释放力量，所以同一个动词既能退烧，也能引导一场座谈。

examples.en: Hire a car of moderate size for a week.
examples.cn: 租一辆中等大小的车用一周。

examples.en: The doctor moderated the dose after the fever dropped.
examples.cn: 退烧之后医生把剂量调低了。

examples.en: She moderated the panel without letting anyone dominate.
examples.cn: 她主持座谈，没让任何人独占话语。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫得瑞特」——做事莫要特别过头，守住中间那一段；记住 moderate 是适度的，也是使缓和、主持讨论。

root: 拉丁语 modus（尺度、方式）派生动词 moderari（守在尺度内），其过去分词 moderatus 构成形容词 moderate；同族词有 moderation、moderator、immoderate。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a kept measure; the senses divide into medium size, calm opinion, a force turned down, and a discussion kept in order.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「守住的尺度」；义项由此分出中等的尺寸、平和的立场、被调低的力量，以及被维持秩序的讨论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing a flame down to a steady, moderate height.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把火苗压到不高不低、稳稳的一档。

branches.en: a car chosen for its middle size on a rental lot
branches.cn: 租车场上挑中的一辆中等尺寸的车

branches.en: two rivals both able to accept one calm position
branches.cn: 两个对手都能接受的一个平和立场

branches.en: a fever curve bending downward after a smaller dose
branches.cn: 减小剂量之后向下弯的体温曲线

branches.en: a hand raised to stop two speakers from talking over each other
branches.cn: 一只举起的手制止两人抢话

branches.en: the same restraint applied to a person and to a force
branches.cn: 同一种克制，一次用于人，一次用于力量

intro.en: The Latin noun for measure supplies the stem, and its verb, participle and four English forms carry the idea of a limit into sizes, opinions and chaired debates.
intro.cn: 拉丁语表示「尺度」的名词提供词干，它的动词、分词与四个英语形式把「界限」这个观念带进尺寸、立场与被主持的辩论。

latinIntro.en: Latin modus, moderari and moderatio form one chain of measure words, and English keeps every link of it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的 modus、moderari 与 moderatio 构成一条「尺度」词链，英语把每一环都保留了下来。

definition_en: belonging to the present age; using the newest methods and design; of art that breaks with tradition; and open rather than old-fashioned in outlook

由 modern 加 -ize 构成，义为「使现代化；更新」
由 modernize 加 -ation 构成，义为「现代化」
由 modern 加 -ist 构成，义为「现代主义者；现代派艺术家」
由 post-（之后）加 modern 构成，义为「后现代的」

senses.title: Belonging to the present age
senses.definition: of the present time or the recent past, as opposed to ancient times
senses.definitionCN: 属于当下或近期的，与古代相对
senses.example: Modern borders in this region were drawn less than a century ago.
senses.exampleCN: 这一地区的现代边界是不到一百年前划定的。
senses.why: Late Latin modernus was built from modo, just now, so the word first pointed at whatever belongs to the moment rather than at a fixed era.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁语 modernus 由 modo（就在此刻）构成，所以这个词原本指向属于当下那一刻的东西，而不是某个固定的时代。

senses.title: Using the newest methods or design
senses.definition: made with the latest techniques or materials, and therefore up to date
senses.definitionCN: 用最新技术或材料做成，因而跟得上时代
senses.example: The clinic replaced its old files with a modern records system.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所把旧档案换成了新式的记录系统。
senses.why: Anything of the present moment can be assumed to use present methods, so modern slid from a label of time to a label of technique.
senses.whyCN: 凡属于当下这一刻的东西，都可假定用了当下的办法，于是 modern 从时间标签滑成了技术标签。

senses.title: Of art that breaks with tradition
senses.definition: belonging to styles of art, music or architecture that deliberately abandon older rules
senses.definitionCN: 属于有意抛弃旧规矩的艺术、音乐或建筑风格
senses.example: The museum's modern wing puzzled visitors who expected marble columns.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的现代派展区让期待大理石柱的观众摸不着头脑。
senses.why: Artists who broke with the academy needed a name for their own work and took the word for the present age, so modern came to mean a deliberate break rather than a date.
senses.whyCN: 反叛学院派的艺术家需要给自家作品一个名号，便借用「当下时代」这个词，于是 modern 指一次有意的断裂，而不只是标一个日期。

senses.title: Open rather than old-fashioned in outlook
senses.definition: willing to accept new ideas about family, work or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 在家事、工作或行为上愿意接受新观念
senses.example: Her modern attitude toward housework surprised her grandparents.
senses.exampleCN: 她对家务的现代态度让祖父母吃惊。
senses.why: If modern means of this moment, a person who keeps up with the moment is called modern in temper, and the word becomes mild praise for being unshackled from old habits.
senses.whyCN: 如果 modern 指「属于此刻」，那么跟上此刻的人就被称为性情 modern；这个词就这样变成了对「不被旧习惯捆住」的一种温和赞许。

intro.en: Modern goes back to Late Latin modernus, formed from modo, just now, plus a suffix of time; it reached English through French and was first used to contrast the present with the ancient world.
intro.cn: modern 可追到晚期拉丁语 modernus，它由 modo（就在此刻）加一个时间后缀构成；经法语进入英语，最初用来把当下与古代世界对照。

items.en: Modo was an adverb meaning just now or only a moment ago, and it supplied the seed of the word for what belongs to the present.
items.cn: modo 是一个副词，意为「就在此刻、刚才」，它为表示「属于当下」的词提供了种子。

items.en: Modernus is usually dated to the fifth century and was built with the time suffix also seen in hodiernus, of today; its coinage is generally thought to set the present against the ancient past.
items.cn: modernus 一般被认为出现于五世纪，用的是与 hodiernus（今天的）相同的时间后缀；一般认为，这个新造词把当下与古代对立起来。

items.en: French used moderne for what belonged to the current age and passed the word to English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语用 moderne 指属于当前时代的东西，并在十六世纪把这个词传入英语。

items.en: English modern first joined the quarrel of the ancients and the moderns, where it meant the writers and scholars of recent times.
items.cn: 英语的 modern 最早出现在「古代人与现代人之争」里，当时指近代的作家与学者。

items.en: Modern English extended the word to technology, to a style of art that rejects old rules, and to people whose views keep pace with the age.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词扩展到技术、反叛旧规矩的艺术风格，以及观念跟得上时代的人。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem and the English derivatives of modern; the near-meaning group gathers words for what belongs to the present moment.
note.cn: 形近组顺着 modern 的拉丁词干与英语派生词展开；近义组收表示「属于当下这一刻」的词。

entries.definition: The condition or quality of being modern.
entries.definitionCN: 处于现代的状态或性质。

entries.definition: To bring something up to present-day standards.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物提升到当今的标准。

entries.definition: A movement in art and letters that broke with older forms.
entries.definitionCN: 在艺术与文学上打破旧形式的运动。

entries.definition: Following and reacting against the modern movement.
entries.definitionCN: 在现当代运动之后并对其作出反应的。

entries.definition: A believer in or maker of modern styles.
entries.definitionCN: 信奉或创作现代风格的人。

entries.definition: Belonging to the same period, or to the present.
entries.definitionCN: 属于同一时期的，或属于当下的。

entries.definition: Happening or existing now.
entries.definitionCN: 现在正在发生或存在的。

entries.definition: Carrying the newest information or design.
entries.definitionCN: 带有最新信息或设计的。

entries.definition: Having happened a short time ago.
entries.definitionCN: 刚刚发生不久的。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a timestamp built on the Latin adverb for just now, and its family keeps dividing into state, action, movement and believer.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起初是用拉丁语「就在此刻」造的一个人时间戳，它的词族不断分成状态、动作、流派与信奉者。

normal.en: Modo, Latin for just now, is the root of modern, so the word is a timestamp before it is a style.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 modo 意为「就在此刻」，它是 modern 的词根，所以这个词先是一个时间戳，然后才是一种风格。

normal.en: The suffix that made modernus belongs to the same time-naming kind as the one in hodiernus, of today, which is why the word reads as belonging to now.
normal.cn: 造出 modernus 的那个后缀，与 hodiernus（今天的）里的时间后缀同类，所以这个词读起来就是「属于现在」。

normal.en: Add -ity for the condition, -ize for the act of updating, -ism for the movement, -ist for the person, so one stem covers state, action, style and believer.
normal.cn: 加 -ity 表状态，加 -ize 表更新的动作，加 -ism 表流派，加 -ist 表人，一个词干覆盖状态、动作、风格与信奉者。

normal.en: Postmodern adds post- to modern, marking a reaction against the very style that modern had named.
normal.cn: postmodern 在 modern 前加 post-，标出对 modern 曾经命名的那种风格的反动。

normal.en: The ancients and the moderns were a real quarrel in European letters, and English modern kept the flavour of taking sides in that argument.
normal.cn: 「古代人与现代人之争」是欧洲文坛上一场真实的争论，英语的 modern 一直留着在那场争论里选边站的味道。

abstract.en: Picture a glass wall going up beside a stone wall, the new one clean and the old one weathered.
abstract.cn: 想象一道玻璃墙在石墙旁边立起，新的干净利落，旧的风化斑驳。

abstract.en: A word that began as a timestamp turns into a judgement: to call something modern is also to say it has left the old rules behind.
abstract.cn: 一个起初只是时间戳的词变成了判断：说某样东西 modern，也是在说它把旧规矩留在了身后。

abstract.en: Every modern thing will one day need a newer word, which is why the vocabulary keeps adding post- and neo- in front of it.
abstract.cn: 每一件 modern 的东西终有一天会需要更新的词，所以词汇不断在它前面加上 post- 与 neo-。

examples.en: Modern borders in this region were drawn less than a century ago.
examples.cn: 这一地区的现代边界是不到一百年前划定的。

examples.en: The clinic replaced its old files with a modern records system.
examples.cn: 诊所把旧档案换成了新式的记录系统。

examples.en: Her modern attitude toward housework surprised her grandparents.
examples.cn: 她对家务的现代态度让祖父母吃惊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩登」——老上海话里的摩登就是时髦，这个词本来就是借来的 modern；记住 modern 是现代的、新式的。

root: 晚期拉丁语 modernus 由 modo（就在此刻）加时间后缀构成，一般认为首见于五世纪；经法语 moderne 进入英语，先指当代的，再指新式、现代派与开明。

sensesIntro.en: The core is belonging to now; the senses divide into a period, a technique, an artistic revolt, and an open outlook.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「属于此刻」；义项由此分出时代、技术、艺术上的反叛，以及开明的观念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass and steel front rising beside an old stone wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面玻璃与钢的立面在旧石墙旁立起。

branches.en: a border line drawn a century ago on an old map
branches.cn: 一张旧地图上不到一百年前划出的边界线

branches.en: paper files replaced by screens in a clinic
branches.cn: 诊所里纸质档案被屏幕取代

branches.en: colour bands on canvas where columns once stood
branches.cn: 画布上的色带，取代了曾经的大理石柱

branches.en: grandparents listening to a granddaughter's plan
branches.cn: 祖父母听孙女讲她的安排

branches.en: the same word for a new machine and a new way of painting
branches.cn: 同一个词，既指新机器，也指新的画法

intro.en: A Latin adverb of the present moment, a time suffix and five English forms carry the word from a date to a style and a temper.
intro.cn: 一个表示当下这一刻的拉丁副词、一个时间后缀，加上五个英语形式，把这个词从日期带到了风格与性情。

latinIntro.en: The reliable Latin core is modo plus the time suffix behind modernus, and hodiernus shows the same pattern of naming what belongs to today.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的拉丁语核心是 modo 加上构成 modernus 的时间后缀，hodiernus 则展示了同样一套「给属于今天的东西命名」的模式。

items.meaningCN: 表示属于某段时间的后缀

definition_zh: 现代化；使社会、经济、制度或设备变得现代的过程；现代化理论；技术更新
definition_en: the process of making a society, economy, institution or equipment modern
core_image: 老厂房里，工人把最后一台手摇车床推出去，换上带屏幕的新机器
scene: 老厂房里，工人把最后一台手摇车床推出去，换上带屏幕的新机器，The factory's modernization replaced hand tools with computer-controlled machines.
sceneCN: 这里 modernization 指「设备与生产的技术更新」（第 3 个义项：技术层面的现代化）；句意为这家工厂的现代化用电脑控制的机器取代了手工工具。图中可辨识物件：手摇车床、带屏幕的新机器、搬运轨道、工人的手套；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 现代化；现代化的过程；技术更新

senses.title: The process of becoming modern
senses.definition: the broad process by which a society acquires modern industry, institutions and ways of life
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会获得现代工业、制度与生活方式的总过程
senses.example: Modernization changed the valley within one generation.
senses.exampleCN: 现代化在一代人的时间里改变了这座山谷。
senses.why: The suffix names a process rather than a state: the word looks at the movement toward modernity, not at modernity itself.
senses.whyCN: 后缀命名的是过程而不是状态：这个词看的是走向现代性的运动，而非现代性本身。

senses.title: The sociological paradigm
senses.definition: the body of theory that explains development as a series of stages from traditional to modern society
senses.definitionCN: 把发展解释为从传统社会到现代社会一系列阶段的理论总体
senses.example: Modernization was the dominant framework in development studies after the war.
senses.exampleCN: 战后，现代化曾是发展研究中的主导框架。
senses.why: A process this large needs a theory, so the same noun names the academic paradigm that tried to describe it.
senses.whyCN: 如此庞大的过程需要理论，因此同一个名词也命名试图描述它的学术范式。

senses.title: Technical upgrading of equipment
senses.definition: the replacement of old machinery, systems or methods with newer and more efficient ones
senses.definitionCN: 用更新、更高效的机器、系统或方法替换旧的
senses.example: The factory's modernization replaced hand tools with computer-controlled machines.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂的现代化用电脑控制的机器取代了手工工具。
senses.why: The grand process has a workshop-sized version: one machine at a time, the old is pushed out and the new is wired in.
senses.whyCN: 宏大的过程有一个车间大小的版本：一次换一台机器，旧的被推出去，新的被接上电线。

senses.title: Urban and infrastructural development
senses.definition: the building of roads, housing, water and power systems to modern standards
senses.definitionCN: 按现代标准建设道路、住房、供水与电力系统
senses.example: Modernization brought the first paved road to the fishing village.
senses.exampleCN: 现代化把第一条铺装路带到了这个渔村。
senses.why: Modern life has a physical shell, and the noun often names the laying of that shell: pipes, wires, asphalt.
senses.whyCN: 现代生活有一层物质外壳，这个名词常指铺这层外壳：管道、电线、沥青。

senses.title: Economic and industrial development
senses.definition: the shift from farming and small craft to industry, wage labour and higher output
senses.definitionCN: 从农业与手工副业转向工业、雇佣劳动与更高产量
senses.example: Economic modernization moved workers from the fields to the mills.
senses.exampleCN: 经济现代化把工人从田里移到了工厂。
senses.why: Economists use the word for the measurable part of the change: where people work and what they produce.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家用这个词指变化中可测量的部分：人在哪里工作、生产什么。

senses.title: Institutional and legal reform
senses.definition: the reform of government, law and administration along modern lines
senses.definitionCN: 按现代方式改革政府、法律与行政
senses.example: Legal modernization removed the old courts and created a written code.
senses.exampleCN: 法律现代化废除了旧法庭，制定了一部成文法典。
senses.why: Industry needs contracts and records, so the process reaches into courts, registries and tax offices.
senses.whyCN: 工业需要合同与记录，因此这一过程延伸到法院、登记处与税务所。

senses.title: Cultural change toward modern values
senses.definition: the spread of values such as mobility, individual choice, science and secular time
senses.definitionCN: 流动性、个人选择、科学与世俗时间观等价值的传播
senses.example: Modernization altered how families arranged marriages and kept time.
senses.exampleCN: 现代化改变了家庭安排婚姻与计算时间的方式。
senses.why: The process is not only machines: it changes what people expect from life and from each other.
senses.whyCN: 这个过程不只是机器：它改变人们对生活、对彼此的期待。

senses.title: The state of being modernized
senses.definition: the result of the process, viewed as a completed condition
senses.definitionCN: 过程的结果，被视为已完成的状态
senses.example: The port's modernization is visible in its cranes and its silence.
senses.exampleCN: 这座港口的现代化在吊车与寂静中都看得见。
senses.why: A process noun can be read backwards as a result: what has been modernized is now a condition.
senses.whyCN: 过程名词也可以倒过来读成结果：已经被现代化的东西，如今成了一种状态。

intro.en: Modernization is modern plus the verb ending -ize and the process ending -ation, ultimately from Late Latin modernus and modo. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: modernization 由 modern 加动词词尾 -ize 与过程词尾 -ation 构成，最终来自晚期拉丁语 modernus 与 modo。年代均为约数。

items.en: Modo meant just now. It is usually derived from modus, measure or manner, though that link is a standard account rather than a recorded certainty.
items.cn: modo 意为「刚刚」。通行说法认为它来自 modus「尺度、方式」，但这一联系只是标准解释，并非有记录的确证。

items.en: Late Latin modernus, of the present time, was built from the time word plus -nus.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 modernus 意为「当下的」，由这个时间词加 -nus 构成。

items.en: The verb ending -ize came through Latin -izare from Greek -izein, meaning to make, practise or become.
items.cn: 动词词尾 -ize 经拉丁语 -izare 来自希腊语 -izein，意为「使、从事或成为」。

items.en: The noun ending -ation came from Latin -atio, which named an action or its result.
items.cn: 名词词尾 -ation 来自拉丁语 -atio，表示动作或其结果。

items.en: Modernization appeared in the nineteenth century as industry and administration began to be described as a single process.
items.cn: modernization 在十九世纪出现，当时工业与行政开始被描述为同一个过程。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use of modernization is not securely dated, and the pre-Latin origin of modo and modus is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定：modernization 在英语中的最早使用没有确切年代；modo 与 modus 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: The first group holds members of the same modern- family; the second holds processes that are often mistaken for modernization itself.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 modern- 词族的成员；第二组是常被误当作现代化本身的过程。

entries.definition: To make something modern; modernization is the process noun built from that verb.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物现代化；modernization 是由该动词构成的过程名词。

entries.definition: Belonging to the present age; it describes a thing, while modernization describes the change that made it so.
entries.definitionCN: 属于当下时代的；它描述事物，而 modernization 描述使之如此的变化。

entries.definition: The state of being modern; modernization is the road, modernity is the place arrived at.
entries.definitionCN: 现代的状态；modernization 是道路，modernity 是抵达的地方。

entries.definition: The artistic and intellectual movement that broke with inherited forms; it is cultural, while modernization is social and technical.
entries.definitionCN: 打破继承形式的艺术与思想运动；它属于文化，而 modernization 属于社会与技术。

entries.definition: Improvement in economic and social conditions; modernization is one model of how development should happen.
entries.definitionCN: 经济与社会状况的改善；现代化是关于发展应如何发生的一种模型。

entries.definition: The growth of manufacturing industry; it is one part of modernization, not the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 制造业的增长；它是现代化的一部分，而非全过程。

entries.definition: Adoption of Western institutions and culture; critics use it to say that modernization was never neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 采纳西方的制度与文化；批评者用它指出现代化从来不是中立的。

entries.definition: An improvement to one machine or system; modernization suggests a broader and longer process.
entries.definitionCN: 对单台机器或系统的改进；modernization 暗示更广、更长的过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real modern stem, the real process endings and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 modern 词干、真实的过程词尾，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: modern plus the make-verb ending and the process ending: the word is literally the making of the modern.
normal.cn: modern 加表示「使……」的动词词尾与表示过程的名词词尾：这个词字面上就是「使现代的过程」。

normal.en: The family runs modern, modernize, modernization, modernity, modernism and modernizer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 modern（现代的）、modernize（使现代化）、modernization（现代化）、modernity（现代性）、modernism（现代主义）、modernizer（推动现代化的人）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: economic modernization, industrial modernization, technical modernization.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：经济现代化、工业现代化、技术现代化。

normal.en: The word is a road, not a destination: modernity is where the road arrives.
normal.cn: 这个词是一条路，不是终点：modernity 才是路抵达的地方。

normal.en: Its common critique is that it treats one model of development as universal.
normal.cn: 对它的常见批评是：它把一种发展模型当作普遍标准。

abstract.en: Picture an old lathe rolled out of a factory while a new machine is wired in.
abstract.cn: 想象一台旧车床被推出厂房，同时一台新机器正在接线。

abstract.en: Picture a village where the first paved road arrives before the first streetlight.
abstract.cn: 想象一个村庄，第一条铺装路先于第一盏路灯到来。

abstract.en: Picture a clock changing from church bells to factory whistles.
abstract.cn: 想象计时方式从教堂钟声变成工厂汽笛。

examples.en: Modernization promised wealth and delivered a new kind of dependence.
examples.cn: 现代化许诺财富，却交出一种新的依赖。

examples.en: The archive's modernization put every ledger online.
examples.cn: 档案馆的现代化把每一本账册都搬上了网。

examples.en: Social modernization changed the wedding more than the factory.
examples.cn: 社会现代化对婚礼的改变，胜过对工厂的改变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩登」加「化」——把旧东西一步步变成摩登的样子，就是现代化。

root: 由 modern 加动词词尾 -ize 与过程词尾 -ation 构成。modern 来自晚期拉丁语 modernus「当下的」，通行说法追溯至 modo「刚刚」，modo 又常被解释为来自 modus「尺度、方式」；-ize 经拉丁语 -izare 源自希腊语 -izein，-ation 来自拉丁语 -atio。modo 与 modus 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one process: a society, a theory, a machine, a road, an economy, a court, a value and finally the finished state.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个过程展开：一个社会、一套理论、一台机器、一条路、一个经济、一座法院、一种价值，最后是完成后的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old machine rolled out while a new one is wired in.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧机器被推出，新机器正在接线。

branches.en: PROCESS AND RESULT: the same word can look forward to the change or backward at what has been changed.
branches.cn: 过程与结果：同一个词既可以向前看变化，也可以回头看在变化之后的状态。

branches.en: THEORY: the process becomes a paradigm that claims to explain all societies.
branches.cn: 理论：这个过程变成一套声称能解释所有社会的范式。

branches.en: MACHINE: the workshop-sized version, one lathe at a time.
branches.cn: 机器：车间大小的版本，一次换一台车床。

branches.en: ROAD AND ECONOMY: pipes, asphalt and wages make the new life possible.
branches.cn: 道路与经济：管道、沥青与工资使新生活成为可能。

branches.en: LAW AND VALUES: courts need written codes, and families need new expectations.
branches.cn: 法律与价值：法院需要成文法典，家庭需要新的期待。

intro.en: Modernization stacks a time adjective, a make-verb ending and a process noun ending.
intro.cn: modernization 叠了一个时间形容词、一个表示「使……」的动词词尾与一个过程名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin modo and modernus supply the adjective, Greek -izein through Latin supplies the verb, and Latin -atio supplies the process noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 modo 与 modernus 提供形容词，希腊语 -izein 经拉丁语提供动词，拉丁语 -atio 提供过程名词。

items.example: The adverb is usually linked to modus, measure.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词通常被联系到 modus「尺度」。

items.example: The adjective entered English through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词经法语进入英语。

items.example: The ending builds modernize and industrialize.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 modernize（使现代化）与 industrialize（使工业化）。

items.example: The ending builds modernization and industrialization.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 modernization（现代化）与 industrialization（工业化）。
现代化改变了这座港口。

items.example: The modernizer rebuilt the telegraph line.
items.exampleCN: 这位现代化推动者重建了电报线。

items.example: Modernity arrived before modernization was complete.
items.exampleCN: 现代性在现代化完成之前就到来了。

items.meaning: the cultural movement of the new
items.example: Modernism changed the gallery, not the factory.
items.exampleCN: 现代主义改变的是画廊，不是工厂。

definition_zh: 谦虚的；适度的；朴素的；端庄的
definition_en: not boasting about one's own abilities or achievements; not large in amount or size; simple and not expensive; decent in dress and behaviour
core_image: 一个人站在人群边上，把自己的成绩轻轻往身后放
scene: 颁奖结束后，年轻人把证书先递给身边的老师，说这份功劳多半是老师给的。The young engineer stayed modest even after the whole team praised her design.
sceneCN: 这里 modest 是「谦虚的」（第 1 个义项：不夸耀自己的能力与成绩）；句意为整个团队称赞她的设计之后，这位年轻工程师仍然保持谦虚。画面里能想见：颁奖台、递出去的证书、站在一旁的老师。

pos.zh: 谦虚的；适度的；朴素的；端庄的

collocations.zh: 微薄的收入；不宽裕的经济条件

derivatives.zh: 由 modest 改词尾为 -y 构成，义为「谦虚；适度；朴素」
由 modest 加 -ly 构成，义为「谦虚地；适度地」
由否定前缀 im- 加 modest 构成，义为「不谦虚的；自夸的」
由 im- 加 modesty 构成，义为「自负；不谦逊」

senses.title: Not boasting about one's abilities or achievements
senses.definition: not talking proudly about your own abilities, successes or importance
senses.definitionCN: 不骄傲地谈论自己的能力、成绩或地位
senses.example: She is modest about the prize and keeps praising her teammates.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这个奖很谦虚，一直在夸队友。
senses.why: Latin modestus was built on modus, a measure; a person who keeps inside the measure does not inflate the space they take up in the room.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 modestus 建立在 modus（尺度）之上；一个守在尺度之内的人，不会把自己在众人面前占的位置吹大。

senses.title: Small in amount, size or degree
senses.definition: not large in amount, size or degree, often pleasantly so
senses.definitionCN: 数量、规模或程度上不大，常带「还算合适」的意味
senses.example: Sales rose by a modest seven percent this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年销售额小幅上升了七个点。
senses.why: The same idea of staying inside a measure applies to numbers: a modest rise is one that does not overshoot the expected line.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「守在尺度内」的想法也能用在数字上：modest 的增长就是没有越过预期那条线的增长。

senses.title: Simple and not expensive
senses.definition: plain and simple, not showy or expensive, especially of clothes, homes or meals
senses.definitionCN: 朴素简单而不张扬、不昂贵，尤指衣着、住所或饭菜
senses.example: They live in a modest flat near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们住在车站附近一套朴素的公寓里。
senses.why: A house that refuses to show off its cost is following the same rule as a person who refuses to show off a trophy.
senses.whyCN: 一座不肯炫耀造价的房子，遵守的规则和一个人不肯炫耀奖杯完全一样。

senses.title: Decent in dress and behaviour, not revealing
senses.definition: of clothes or behaviour, avoiding anything that draws sexual attention
senses.definitionCN: 指衣着或举止避开会引起性方面注意的东西
senses.example: The school asks students to wear modest clothing.
senses.exampleCN: 学校要求学生穿端庄的衣着。
senses.why: Here the measure is social: clothing that stays within what a situation allows covers the body instead of inviting stares.
senses.whyCN: 这里的尺度是社会性的：守在场合适度的衣着遮住身体，而不招来盯视。

intro.en: Modest goes back to a Latin word for keeping to a measure, and French passed it into English as a word about restraint rather than size.
intro.cn: modest 可追到拉丁语中「守尺度」的说法，法语把它传入英语时，谈的是节制，而不是大小。

items.en: Modus meant a measure, a limit or a way of doing something, and it is the root behind mode, moderate and modest.
items.cn: modus 意为尺度、限度或做事的门径，是 mode、moderate 与 modest 共同的词根。

items.en: Modestus described someone who stayed within due measure, sober in manner and free of swagger.
items.cn: modestus 形容守分寸的人：举止有节、不张狂。

items.en: Modestia named that quality itself, the habit of not claiming more than one's share.
items.cn: modestia 指这种品质本身，即不多占、不越界的习惯。

items.en: French took the adjective as modeste and used it for people, manners and later for plain, unshowy things.
items.cn: 法语把形容词写作 modeste，先用于人和举止，后来也用于朴素、不张扬的事物。

items.en: English extended the word from humble speech to small amounts, simple homes and decent clothing.
items.cn: 英语把这个词从谦逊的言谈扩展到小额数量、简朴住所与端庄衣着。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin measure root and its English family; the near-meaning group gathers words for humility, smallness and plainness.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语「尺度」词根及其英语词族展开；近义组收表示谦逊、少量与朴素的词。

entries.definition: The noun for the habit of not boasting, and for plainness in dress.
entries.definitionCN: 不夸耀的习惯，也指衣着朴素；是 modest 的名词形式。

entries.definition: In a humble or moderate way.
entries.definitionCN: 谦虚地；适度地。

entries.definition: Boastful, or too revealing in dress.
entries.definitionCN: 自夸的，或衣着过于暴露的。

entries.definition: Keeping within limits, neither too much nor too little.
entries.definitionCN: 守在中庸之内的；不过分也不欠缺的。

entries.definition: A way or manner of doing something, from the same Latin measure word.
entries.definitionCN: 做事的方式、门径，来自同一个表示尺度的拉丁词。

entries.definition: Having a low opinion of your own importance.
entries.definitionCN: 对自己的重要性评价低；谦逊的。

entries.definition: Neither very large nor very small.
entries.definitionCN: 既不大也不小的；中等的。

entries.definition: Simple, with no decoration or display.
entries.definitionCN: 简单的，没有装饰或炫耀的。

entries.definition: Not drawing attention to yourself or your merits.
entries.definitionCN: 不引人注意自己的功劳的；不摆架子的。

normalIntro.en: The word grows out of a Latin word for measure, and its whole family keeps asking whether someone or something stays inside its proper size.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词长在拉丁语表示「尺度」的词上，整个词族反复在问：人或者事物有没有守在自己该有的大小里。

normal.en: Modus is Latin for a measure or limit, so modest begins as a judgement about staying inside the line.
normal.cn: modus 是拉丁语的「尺度、限度」，所以 modest 起初是对「有没有守在线内」的判断。

normal.en: Modesty swaps the -est ending for -y, the same pattern as honest and honesty.
normal.cn: modesty 把 -est 词尾换成 -y，和 honest 变 honesty 是同一种构词方式。

normal.en: im- can negate: immodest is the person who claims more than their measure allows.
normal.cn: im- 可以表否定：immodest 就是占了超出自己尺度的位置的人。

normal.en: Modest about praise, modest rise, modest flat: one word measures claims, numbers and housing alike.
normal.cn: 对赞美谦虚、小幅增长、朴素公寓：同一个词在衡量说法、数字和住处。

normal.en: In clothing, modest marks what stays covered instead of inviting attention.
normal.cn: 用在衣着上，modest 标记的是遮蔽得宜、不招来注视的那种穿法。

abstract.en: Think of a person who could take up the whole stage but chooses one small square of it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人本可以占满整个舞台，却只挑了一小块地方站。

abstract.en: A modest number behaves like a polite guest: it arrives without filling the room.
abstract.cn: 一个不大的数字像有礼貌的客人：来了，但不把屋子塞满。

abstract.en: Measuring is the quiet act behind the word, and every sense is a different ruler.
abstract.cn: 「量」是这个词背后的动作，而每个义项都换了一把不同的尺子。

examples.en: She is modest about the prize and keeps praising her teammates.
examples.cn: 她对这个奖很谦虚，一直在夸队友。

examples.en: They live in a modest flat near the station.
examples.cn: 他们住在车站附近一套朴素的公寓里。

examples.en: The school asks students to wear modest clothing.
examples.cn: 学校要求学生穿端庄的衣着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩的」——骑摩的的师傅挣得不多，日子过得朴实，也不吹牛；modest 就是适度、朴素、谦虚。

root: 拉丁语 modus（尺度、限度）派生出 modestus（守分寸的），再经法语 modeste 进入英语；同族词都与尺度、节制有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is staying inside a measure; the senses apply that measure to claims about oneself, to quantity, to possessions and to the body.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是守在尺度之内；义项把同一把尺子依次用在自我评价、数量、财物和身体上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing at the edge of a group, quietly putting her own achievement behind her back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在人群边上，把自己的成绩悄悄藏到身后。

branches.en: a winner who names the people who helped
branches.cn: 获奖者说出帮助过自己的人

branches.en: a sales chart rising by one small step
branches.cn: 销售曲线只抬高一小格

branches.en: a plain flat with bare walls and one lamp
branches.cn: 白墙素灯的一间小屋

branches.en: a meal served without decoration or display
branches.cn: 一顿不作摆盘的饭菜

branches.en: a school rule about sleeves and hemlines
branches.cn: 关于袖长与下摆的校规

intro.en: A Latin measure word, a quality noun, a French adjective and three English endings carry modest from a ruler to a manner of speech, a size and a dress code.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语「尺度」词、一个表品质的名词、一个法语形容词和三个英语词尾，把 modest 从一把尺子带到了说话方式、尺寸和衣着规范。

latinIntro.en: Modus and modestia are recorded Latin words, and the adjective modestus is built on them; the family carries the idea of a limit.
latinIntro.cn: modus 与 modestia 都是有记录的拉丁词，形容词 modestus 由它们构成；这一族词都带着「限度」的观念。

items.meaningCN: 形容词词尾：具有……性质的

definition_zh: 修改；调整；修饰；缓和；修订；改性
definition_en: to change something in some details or qualities without replacing it entirely, often to make it fit a new purpose or to make it less extreme
core_image: 在一件旧物上按尺寸修整几处，整体仍然是原来那件东西
scene: 工程师没有换掉整只阀门，只改了一个法兰让它接上新管道。The engineer did not replace the whole valve; she chose to modify one flange so that it would fit the new pipe.
sceneCN: 这里 modify 是「部分修改」（第 1 个义项：改动局部而不整体替换）；句意：工程师没有换掉整个阀门，只改动了一个法兰盘，让它能接上新管道。场景要点：一台拆开的旧阀门、一只被换掉的零件、旁边保留完好的阀体；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 修改；调整；修饰；缓和；修订

senses.title: Change a part, not the whole
senses.definition: to change some details, parts, or qualities of something while leaving its identity and main structure intact
senses.definitionCN: 改动某物的部分细节、部件或性质，同时保留它的身份与主要结构
senses.example: The engineer modified the valve instead of replacing the whole assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师改动了阀门，而不是更换整个组件。
senses.why: Latin modificare joined modus 'measure' to facere 'make': to make according to a measure. The word starts from adjusting a thing's proportions, not from destroying and remaking it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 modificare 把 modus“尺度”与 facere“做”合在一起：按尺度去制作。这个词的起点是调整一件东西的比例，而不是毁掉重造。

senses.title: Adapt to fit a new use
senses.definition: to adjust something so that it suits a different purpose, condition, or user
senses.definitionCN: 调整某物，使其适合不同的目的、条件或使用者
senses.example: The school modified its timetable to fit the bus schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 学校调整了课程表，以配合公交时刻。
senses.why: A measure is taken against a purpose. When the purpose changes, the thing is re-measured and trimmed until it fits again, which is why modify often appears with 'to fit' or 'for'.
senses.whyCN: 尺度总是对着某个目的量。目的变了，东西就被重新量一遍、修一遍，直到重新合身，所以 modify 常与“适应”“为了”一类说法连用。

senses.title: Grammar: a word limits another
senses.titleCN: 语法：一个词限定另一个词
senses.definition: of a word or phrase, to limit or qualify the meaning of another word
senses.definitionCN: 指一个词或短语限定或说明另一个词的意义
senses.example: In 'a red door', the adjective modifies the noun 'door'.
senses.exampleCN: 在 a red door 中，形容词修饰名词 door。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the word for narrowing a meaning. An adjective places a measure on a noun, saying which part of its range is meant, without replacing the noun.
senses.whyCN: 语法学借这个词来表示收窄意义。形容词给名词加上一个尺度，说明指的是它范围里的哪一部分，而不替换这个名词。

senses.title: Soften a claim or tone
senses.definition: to make a statement, demand, or tone less absolute or less severe
senses.definitionCN: 使陈述、要求或语气不那么绝对、不那么严厉
senses.example: He modified his tone when he saw that the child was listening.
senses.exampleCN: 看到孩子在听，他把语气缓和了下来。
senses.why: To keep within measure also means not to exceed it. A demand that is modified has been brought back inside reasonable bounds, so the word can mean 'soften' rather than 'change'.
senses.whyCN: 保持在尺度之内，也意味着不越过尺度。被 modify 的要求被拉回到合理的范围内，所以这个词可以表示“缓和”，而不只是“改变”。

senses.title: Amend a legal text
senses.definition: to make a formal, limited change to a law, contract, or official document
senses.definitionCN: 对法律、合同或正式文件作有限度的正式改动
senses.example: The council modified the payment clause but left the rest of the contract untouched.
senses.exampleCN: 理事会修改了付款条款，但合同其余部分未动。
senses.why: A legal document is changed clause by clause, never rewritten wholesale if it can be helped. Modify is the natural verb for a bounded edit that leaves the instrument in force.
senses.whyCN: 法律文件是一条款一条款地改，不到万不得已不会整份重写。modify 正是表示这种有限改动、让文件继续有效的动词。

senses.title: Change a setting or file
senses.definition: in computing, to change the contents, settings, or code of a file or system
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，改动文件或系统的内容、设置或代码
senses.example: Do not modify the system files without a backup.
senses.exampleCN: 没有备份时不要修改系统文件。
senses.why: Software is a structure with many settable measures. Editing one setting or one line modifies the system: the rest keeps running, which is exactly the partial-change picture.
senses.whyCN: 软件是一个有许多可调尺度的结构。改一项设置或一行代码就是 modify 系统：其余部分照旧运行，这正是“局部改动”的画面。

senses.title: Rewrite a gene
senses.definition: in biology, to change an organism's genetic material, often to give it a new trait
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学中，改变生物体的遗传物质，常为赋予它新的性状
senses.example: The scientists modified one gene in the rice plant to resist drought.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家改动了水稻的一个基因，使其抗旱。
senses.why: The organism is not replaced; one instruction inside it is re-measured and rewritten. The phrase 'genetically modified' keeps the sense of a targeted edit to an existing living thing.
senses.whyCN: 生物体本身没有被替换，被改写的是它内部的一条指令。“genetically modified”这一说法保留了“对既有生物做定点改动”的意思。

senses.title: Alter a material's surface
senses.definition: in materials science, to change the properties of a surface or structure without changing its bulk
senses.definitionCN: 在材料科学中，改变表面或结构的性能，而不改变其主体
senses.example: The coating modifies the surface without changing the bulk of the metal.
senses.exampleCN: 这层涂层改变了金属的表面性能，却没有改变其主体。
senses.why: Here the measure is applied only to the skin of the object. The bulk stays as it was, which makes modify the right verb for a treatment rather than a replacement.
senses.whyCN: 这里的尺度只施加在物体的表皮上。主体保持原样，因此 modify 适合表示一种处理，而不是替换。

senses.title: A sound changed by its neighbour
senses.titleCN: 语音受邻音影响而变化
senses.definition: in phonetics, of a sound, to be changed under the influence of a neighbouring sound
senses.definitionCN: 在语音学中，指一个音受相邻音影响而发生改变
senses.example: In rapid speech, the final sound is often modified by the sound that follows it.
senses.exampleCN: 在快速语流中，末尾的音常被后面的音改变。
senses.why: A sound keeps its identity but shifts its shape to fit its neighbours, just as a part is trimmed to fit a new pipe. The word's 'fit' sense is at work even here.
senses.whyCN: 一个音保留自己的身份，却改变形状去适应相邻的音，正如一个零件被修整以接上新管道。即便在这里，这个词“适配”的意思仍在起作用。

intro.en: Modify entered English from Old French in the late fourteenth century and goes back to Latin modificare, literally 'to make by measure'. Its two Latin parts, modus and facere, explain why it means partial adjustment rather than total replacement. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: modify 在 14 世纪晚期从古法语进入英语，可追溯到拉丁语 modificare，字面意为“按尺度制作”。它的两个拉丁成分 modus 与 facere，解释了它为何表示局部调整而不是整体替换。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded as modifien, 'alter, amend, adjust, change the properties, form, or function of'. It also meant 'set limits, keep within the bounds of reason; choose a middle course'.
items.cn: 最早记录为 modifien，意为“改变、修正、调整、改变……的性质、形式或功能”。它还有“设定界限、保持在理性范围之内、选择中间道路”的意思。

items.en: The English verb came through Old French modifier (14c.), which already carried the sense of altering something to fit.
items.cn: 这个英语动词经古法语 modifier（14 世纪）而来，后者已经带有“改动某物使其适配”的意思。

items.en: Latin modificare meant 'to limit, measure off, restrain'. It joined modus 'measure, manner' with the combining form of facere 'to make'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 modificare 意为“限定、量出、约束”。它把 modus“尺度、方式”与 facere“制作”的结合形式合在一起。

items.en: Modus goes back to PIE *med- 'take appropriate measures', the root behind mode, moderate, and modest. Facere goes back to PIE *dhe- 'to set, put', the root behind do and deed.
items.cn: modus 可追溯到原始印欧语 *med-“采取恰当的尺度”，也是 mode、moderate、modest 的词根。facere 可追溯到原始印欧语 *dhe-“放置、安放”，也是 do 与 deed 的词根。

items.en: Modification is recorded c. 1500 in philosophy, 'determination by a mode or quality'. Modifier appears in the 1580s as 'one who or that which modifies'; its grammatical sense is from 1865. The 'result of a variation' sense of modification is from the 1660s, and 'act of altering' from 1774.
items.cn: modification 约 1500 年出现在哲学中，意为“由某种模式或性质所决定”。modifier 于 16 世纪 80 年代出现，指“修改者或修改之物”；其语法义始于 1865 年。modification 的“变化结果”义始于 17 世纪 60 年代，“改变的行为”义始于 1774 年。

items.en: Moderate comes from Latin moderari 'keep within measure', the same *med- root but a different branch. Adjust comes from Old French ajouster, from Late Latin adjuxtare 'bring near'. Alter comes from Latin alter 'the other of two'. Each changes something in a different direction or degree.
items.cn: moderate 来自拉丁语 moderari“保持在尺度之内”，同出 *med- 词根，但属于另一分支。adjust 来自古法语 ajouster，源于晚期拉丁语 adjuxtare“使靠近”。alter 来自拉丁语 alter“两者中的另一个”。它们各自以不同方向或不同程度改变事物。

note.en: The first group separates the noun, the agent, and the two participles built on modify; the second compares verbs of change that learners too often use as exact synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组把由 modify 构成的名词、施动者与两个分词分开；第二组比较学习者常当作完全同义词的几个“改变”动词。

entries.definition: a change made to something, or the act of changing it. It names the change or the process, while modify names the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物所作的改动，或改动这一行为。它命名改动或过程，而 modify 命名动作本身。

entries.definition: one who or that which modifies; in grammar, a word that limits another word. It is the doer or the tool, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 修改者或修改之物；语法中指限定另一词的词。它是施动者或工具，不是动作。

entries.definition: changed in some parts, as in 'genetically modified' or 'a modified version'. It describes the result, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 局部被改动的，如“转基因的”或“修改过的版本”。它描述结果，而不是过程。

entries.definition: not changed at all. The un- prefix marks the absence of exactly the partial edit that modify performs.
entries.definitionCN: 完全未被改动的。un- 前缀标记的正是 modify 所做的那种局部改动的缺席。

entries.definition: to change something slightly so that it fits, works, or looks right. It stresses fitting a standard or a position, while modify can also mean changing a design or a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 轻微改变某物，使其合适、正常或位置正确。它强调对准某个标准或位置，而 modify 还可指改动设计或规则。

entries.definition: to make something different, often in a way that changes its character or appearance. It is broader and can suggest a deeper change than modify.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物不同，常指改变其性质或外观。它范围更广，也可能暗示比 modify 更深的改变。

entries.definition: to change a text, law, or agreement in order to correct or improve it. It is mostly formal and textual, whereas modify also covers objects and behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 为纠正或改进而改动文本、法律或协议。它多用于正式文本，而 modify 也覆盖物件与行为。

entries.definition: to make something less extreme or less intense, or to preside over a discussion. It shares the 'measure' root but works mainly on strength, not on form.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物不那么极端或强烈，或主持讨论。它与 modify 共享“尺度”词根，但主要作用于强度，而不是形式。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin modus 'measure' plus facere 'make', and the English family modification, modifier, mode, and moderate.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 modus“尺度”加 facere“制作”，以及英语词族 modification、modifier、mode、moderate。

normal.en: modus is 'measure' and -ify comes from facere 'make'. To modify is to make according to a measure, which is why the thing keeps its identity.
normal.cn: modus 是“尺度”，-ify 来自 facere“制作”。modify 就是按尺度去制作，所以被改的东西保留自己的身份。

normal.en: The Latin verb also meant 'set limits, keep within bounds', so modifying a demand can mean softening it rather than changing its content.
normal.cn: 这个拉丁动词还意为“设定界限、保持在范围之内”，所以修改一项要求可以是把它放缓，而不是改变内容。

normal.en: modification is the change or the act; modifier is the person or word that does it; modified is the result.
normal.cn: modification 是改动或改动行为；modifier 是做这件事的人或词；modified 是结果。

normal.en: mode, moderate, modest and modify all share *med- 'take appropriate measures', but only modify adds the 'make' part.
normal.cn: mode、moderate、modest、modify 都共享 *med-“采取恰当尺度”，但只有 modify 加了“制作”这一部分。

normal.en: In grammar the word narrows meaning: an adjective modifies a noun without replacing it, the same partial-change picture.
normal.cn: 在语法里这个词收窄意义：形容词修饰名词而不替换它，仍是那幅“局部改动”的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a craftsman with a ruler beside an old chair. He shaves one leg, keeps the frame, and the chair is still the same chair.
abstract.cn: 想象一位工匠把尺子放在一把旧椅子旁。他刨短一条腿，保留框架，椅子仍是同一把椅子。

abstract.en: Modify is a dial, not a switch: it turns the value a little, while replace would swap the whole unit out.
abstract.cn: modify 是一个旋钮，不是开关：它把数值稍微转动一点，而 replace 会把整个部件换掉。

abstract.en: Every modified thing still answers to its old name; if it no longer does, it was not modified but replaced.
abstract.cn: 每一件被 modify 的东西仍回应它原来的名字；如果它不再回应，那它不是被修改，而是被替换了。

examples.en: We modified the proposal after the first round of comments.
examples.cn: 第一轮意见之后，我们修改了提案。

examples.en: The app lets you modify the layout without changing the underlying data.
examples.cn: 这个应用允许你修改布局，而不改动底层数据。

examples.en: Some crops were modified to grow in salt water, but the yield remains low.
examples.cn: 有些作物被改造为能在咸水中生长，但产量仍然很低。

dict_mnemonic.text: “摸得改”——先摸清原有尺寸，再动手改那几处，整体不换 → modify 修改、调整（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 modificare“按尺度制作”，由 modus“尺度”加 facere“制作”构成，核心是“按尺寸修整局部，而不整体替换”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of modify, all from one gesture: a measure is laid on an existing thing and a few parts are trimmed, while the thing itself remains what it was.
sensesIntro.cn: modify 的九个义项都来自同一个动作：把尺子放在既有之物上，修整其中几处，而物件本身仍是原来的物件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a few parts trimmed to measure, the whole left standing.
core.cn: 核心意象：按尺寸修整几处，整体仍然立着。

branches.en: PARTIAL CHANGE: details or parts are re-measured, either to improve the thing or to fit a new use.
branches.cn: 局部改变：细节或部件被重新量过，或为改良物件，或为适配新用途。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: a word places a measure on another word and narrows its meaning without replacing it.
branches.cn: 语法：一个词给另一个词加上尺度，收窄它的意义，而不替换它。

branches.en: BOUNDS AND TEXT: a tone or demand is brought back inside measure, and a legal clause is edited while the document stays in force.
branches.cn: 尺度与文本：语气或要求被拉回尺度之内，法律条款被改动而文件继续有效。

branches.en: SYSTEMS AND GENES: one setting, one line of code, or one gene is changed while the rest keeps running.
branches.cn: 系统与基因：一项设置、一行代码或一个基因被改动，其余部分照旧运行。

branches.en: SURFACE AND SOUND: only the skin of a material, or the shape of a sound, is adjusted to fit its surroundings.
branches.cn: 表面与语音：只调整材料的表皮或一个音的形状，使其适应周围环境。

intro.en: Modify is a Latin verb whose English shape joins mod- 'measure' to -ify 'make'. The same stem, with -ation, -er, -ed, -able and un-, produces the rest of the family.
intro.cn: modify 是拉丁语动词，其英语形态把 mod-“尺度”与 -ify“制作”合在一起。同一词干加上 -ation、-er、-ed、-able 与 un-，构成其余词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin modificare combined modus 'measure' and facere 'make'. Facere also gives -fic-, -fect, and -fy in English, which is why modify, manufacture, and effect all contain a 'making' piece.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 modificare 把 modus“尺度”与 facere“制作”合起来。facere 在英语里还给出 -fic-、-fect 与 -fy，所以 modify、manufacture、effect 都含有一个“制作”的成分。

items.meaning: to make according to measure; to change in part
items.meaningCN: 按尺度制作；局部改变（mod- 尺度 + -ify 使……）
items.example: They modified the engine to burn less fuel.
items.exampleCN: 他们改动了发动机，使其更省油。

items.meaning: a change, or the act of changing
items.meaningCN: 修改；改动（-ation 构成行为名词）
items.example: The design needs only a small modification.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计只需要做一处小改动。

items.meaning: one who modifies; a grammatical qualifier
items.meaningCN: 修改者；修饰语（-er 表施动者）
items.example: In the phrase 'very cold', 'very' is a modifier.
items.exampleCN: 在 very cold 这一短语中，very 是修饰语。

items.meaningCN: 被局部改动的（-ed 构成过去分词）
items.exampleCN: 修改后的版本运行得更快。

items.meaningCN: 未修改的（un- 否定 + modified）
items.example: The control group used unmodified seed.
items.exampleCN: 对照组使用的是未经改造的种子。

items.example: The settings are modifiable by the user.
items.exampleCN: 这些设置可由用户修改。

items.meaning: a user-made change to a game
items.meaningCN: 模组；游戏修改版（modification 的截短）
items.example: He installed a mod that adds new maps.
items.exampleCN: 他安装了一个增加新地图的模组。

items.example: The device has a low-power mode.
items.exampleCN: 这个设备有一个低功耗模式。

items.meaning: kept within measure; to reduce intensity
items.meaningCN: 适度的；使缓和（保持在尺度内）
items.example: She moderated her criticism in public.
items.exampleCN: 她在公开场合缓和了自己的批评。

items.meaning: a person's usual way of working
items.meaningCN: 一贯做法；做事方式（拉丁语“工作的方式”）
items.example: The thief's modus operandi was always the same.
items.exampleCN: 这个窃贼的作案手法始终如一。

items.meaning: to treat something as a commodity
items.meaningCN: 使商品化（com- 共同 + mod- 尺度 + -ify 使……）
items.example: Critics say the festival has commodified local music.
items.exampleCN: 批评者说这个节日把本地音乐商品化了。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 限定；量出；约束（modus 尺度 + facere 制作）

definition_zh: 微湿的；湿润的；潮湿的；（食物）湿润柔软的
definition_en: slightly wet, especially in a soft or pleasant way rather than soaked
core_image: 刚拧过的毛巾还留着水痕，摸上去凉而柔，却不会滴下水来
scene: 面包师把一块微湿的布盖在面团上，布面只是潮潮的。The baker laid a moist cloth over the dough.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「带少量水、微湿而不滴水」（第 1 个义项：表面轻微湿润）；句意为面包师把一块微湿的布盖在面团上；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 微湿的；湿润的；（气候）潮湿的；（食物）湿润柔软的

senses.title: Slightly wet to the touch
senses.definition: slightly wet, with enough water to be felt but not enough to drip
senses.definitionCN: 带有一点可被摸出的水，但还不到往下滴的程度
senses.example: The baker laid a moist cloth over the dough.
senses.exampleCN: 面包师把一块微湿的布盖在面团上。
senses.why: Moist is the adjective of the moisture family, so it describes the state of holding a small amount of water, never being soaked.
senses.whyCN: moist 是 moisture 词族的形容词，描述「持有少量水」的状态，而不是被水浸透。

senses.title: Soil that holds water for roots
senses.titleCN: 能保住水供根系吸收的土壤
senses.definition: soil that is damp enough for plants to draw water from it
senses.definitionCN: 湿润到足以让植物从其中吸水生长的土壤
senses.example: Seedlings grow fastest in moist soil.
senses.exampleCN: 幼苗在湿润的土壤里长得最快。
senses.why: A surface that holds the right amount of water is good ground; the same adjective follows the water into the earth.
senses.whyCN: 恰好留住适量水的表面就是好土地；同一个形容词跟着水走进了泥土。

senses.title: Air carrying water vapour
senses.definition: air that contains noticeable water vapour, often warm and heavy
senses.definitionCN: 含有明显水汽、常显得温暖沉闷的空气
senses.example: A moist wind blew in from the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵潮湿的风从海上吹来。
senses.why: Air can be wet without being liquid, so moist here describes what the air holds rather than what it touches.
senses.whyCN: 空气可以非液态地「湿」着，所以这里的 moist 描述空气所含之物，而不是它碰到的东西。

senses.title: Food with a soft, wet texture
senses.definition: food that is soft and retains water, usually said with approval
senses.definitionCN: 柔软并保住了水的食物，通常带赞许意味
senses.example: The cake stays moist for three days.
senses.exampleCN: 这块蛋糕能保持湿润三天。
senses.why: For bakers, dryness is the fault and moisture the virtue, so moist became a word of praise on a menu.
senses.whyCN: 对烘焙者来说，干是缺点、湿是优点，于是 moist 成了菜单上的褒词。

senses.title: Eyes filled with tears
senses.definition: eyes that are wet because tears are rising in them
senses.definitionCN: 因泪水涌起而显得湿的眼睛
senses.example: Her eyes grew moist when the letter was read aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 信被大声念出来时，她的眼睛湿了。
senses.why: The body's own water shows an inner state; the adjective moves from weather and food to feeling.
senses.whyCN: 身体里的水显露内心状态，这个形容词于是从天气与食物走到了情感。

senses.title: A damp climate or season
senses.definition: a climate or season with persistently damp air
senses.definitionCN: 空气长期潮湿的气候或季节
senses.example: The valley has a moist climate that suits ferns.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷气候潮湿，很适合蕨类生长。
senses.why: When dampness lasts long enough to define a place, the word becomes a description of climate.
senses.whyCN: 当潮湿持续得足以定义一个地方时，这个词就成了对气候的描述。

senses.title: Tissue kept from drying out
senses.definition: in medicine and skin care, tissue kept in its natural damp state
senses.definitionCN: 医学与护肤语境中，保持在天然湿润状态的组织
senses.example: Keep the wound moist while it heals.
senses.exampleCN: 伤口愈合期间要保持湿润。
senses.why: Medical writers borrowed the plain adjective to mean 'not allowed to dry', the same idea applied to a patient.
senses.whyCN: 医学写作借用了这个普通形容词，表示「不让变干」，只是把同一想法用到病人身上。

senses.title: Moist heat in cooking and therapy
senses.definition: heat carried by steam or water rather than by dry air
senses.definitionCN: 由蒸汽或水而非干热空气传导的热
senses.example: Braising cooks the meat with moist heat.
senses.exampleCN: 炖煮用湿热把肉做熟。
senses.why: Here moist does not describe an object but a medium: heat that travels with water.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 moist 不描述物体，而描述介质：随水一起传导的热。

intro.en: Moist comes from Old French and its Latin background is contested. The reconstruction is labelled as a hypothesis; the word's deeper source is marked as source uncertain.
intro.cn: moist 来自古法语，其拉丁背景存在争议。重构形式已标注为假说；更深来源不确定。

items.en: Old French moiste meant 'wet, damp, fresh', and also 'newly made, still soft', a range wider than the modern English word.
items.cn: 古法语 moiste 意为「湿的、潮湿的、新鲜的」，也有「刚做成、仍柔软的」义，范围比现代英语更宽。

items.en: English took moiste as moist and used it for damp air, damp earth and food that had not dried out.
items.cn: 英语借入为 moist，用于潮湿的空气、湿润的土地和没有变干的食物。

items.en: The common reconstruction is Vulgar Latin *muscidus 'mouldy', an altered form of Latin mucidus. The alteration is assumed, not attested.
items.cn: 常见重构是俗拉丁语 *muscidus「发霉的」，为拉丁语 mucidus 的变形。这一变形是假定，并无文献记录。

items.en: Other scholars link the Romance family to Latin madidus 'wet, soaked' and madere 'to be wet'. The two hypotheses are usually presented together rather than decided.
items.cn: 另一些学者把这一罗曼语词族联系到拉丁语 madidus「湿透的」与 madere「潮湿」。两种假说通常并列陈述，不作定论。

items.en: The 'eyes wet with tears' use appears in the sixteenth century, and the approving culinary use became common in the nineteenth.
items.cn: 「眼睛含泪」的用法出现于十六世纪，带赞许意味的烹饪用法在十九世纪变得常见。

note.en: Group one holds short words that look or sound close to moist; group two holds adjectives that also describe water.
note.cn: 第一组是与 moist 字形或读音接近的短词；第二组是也描述水分的形容词。

entries.definition: The superlative of much or many. It has a long vowel and ends in -st, and comes from Old English mǣst, not from the moist family.
entries.definitionCN: much 或 many 的最高级。元音较长，词尾是 -st，源自古英语 mǣst，与 moist 词族无关。

entries.definition: To lift something with ropes or a machine. The vowel is /ɔɪ/ and the first consonant is h-, so the two words are not related.
entries.definitionCN: 用绳索或机械把某物升起。元音是 /ɔɪ/，首辅音是 h-，两词没有词源关系。

entries.definition: A modal verb of obligation, or the juice of crushed grapes. The vowel is /ʌ/ and the meaning has nothing to do with dampness.
entries.definitionCN: 表示义务的情态动词，或压碎的葡萄汁。元音是 /ʌ/，意义与潮湿无关。

entries.definition: Slightly wet, usually in a way that feels cold or unpleasant; damp often criticises where moist may praise.
entries.definitionCN: 微湿，通常带阴冷或不适感；damp 常带批评，而 moist 可能带赞许。

entries.definition: Describing air or weather that holds a lot of water vapour, usually oppressively so; it applies to air, rarely to cake.
entries.definitionCN: 形容空气或天气含水汽多，常令人闷热；它用于空气，很少用于蛋糕。

entries.definition: Covered or soaked with liquid water; it is stronger than moist and implies visible water or a thorough soaking.
entries.definitionCN: 被液态水覆盖或浸透；比 moist 更强，暗示可见的水或彻底浸湿。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes and real compounds, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：使用真实的后缀与真实的复合词，不编造顺口溜。

normal.en: moist is the adjective, moisture is the noun: remove the -ure noun ending and you are left with the describing word.
normal.cn: moist 是形容词，moisture 是名词：去掉名词后缀 -ure，就剩下那个描述性的词。

normal.en: moisten adds -en 'make', the same pattern as deepen and strengthen, so it means 'make moist'.
normal.cn: moisten 加 -en「使……」，与 deepen、strengthen 同构，所以就是「使湿润」。

normal.en: moistness is moist plus -ness, the standard suffix for a quality, as in kindness and darkness.
normal.cn: moistness 是 moist 加 -ness，这是表示性质的标准后缀，如 kindness、darkness。

normal.en: moist heat is a real cooking term opposed to dry heat: braising and steaming use steam, roasting and grilling use dry air.
normal.cn: moist heat 是真实的烹饪术语，与 dry heat 相对：炖、蒸用蒸汽，烤、炙用干热空气。

normal.en: moist eyes is a common written phrase for tears about to fall, linking a physical film of water to emotion.
normal.cn: moist eyes 是常见的书面搭配，指快要落下的眼泪，把一层水的物理薄膜与情绪连在一起。

abstract.en: Abstractly, moist is water below the dripping point: enough to be felt, not enough to fall. Symbol: a towel that leaves a print on the table but no puddle.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，moist 是还没到滴落点的水：足以被感觉到，却不足以落下来。符号：一条在桌上留下印子却没有积水的毛巾。

abstract.en: The same 'just enough water' can be praise in a cake, a warning in a wall, and tenderness in an eye.
abstract.cn: 同样的「恰好够的水」，在蛋糕里是赞美，在墙里是警告，在眼睛里是柔情。

abstract.en: So moist never means soaked; it always means a small, contained, often welcome amount.
abstract.cn: 所以 moist 从不表示浸透，而总是表示少量、被收住、往往还是受欢迎的一份水。

examples.en: Turn the soil while it is still moist but not muddy.
examples.cn: 趁土还湿润但没变成泥的时候翻土。

examples.en: A moist towel is better than a dry one for cleaning up dust.
examples.cn: 擦灰时用湿毛巾比干毛巾好用。

examples.en: The air felt moist before the storm arrived.
examples.cn: 暴风雨来临前，空气显得潮乎乎的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「抹湿」：抹布一抹，桌面就湿了 → moist 微湿的

root: 古法语 moiste「湿的」；其拉丁来源有争议，通常重构为俗拉丁语 *muscidus（源自拉丁 mucidus「发霉的」），也有学者联系 madere「潮湿」，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one idea: water just below the dripping point. The word starts at a surface, then enters soil, air, food, eyes, climate, healing tissue and finally a cooking medium.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个意思展开：还没到滴落点的水。这个词从表面开始，随后进入土壤、空气、食物、眼睛、气候、愈合中的组织，最后成为一种烹饪介质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surface that is cool and slightly dark with water but never drips.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块被水弄得发凉、颜色略深、却始终不滴水的表面。

branches.en: A FILM OF WATER: plain touch and medical care both describe tissue that holds a little water.
branches.cn: 一层水膜：日常触摸与医疗护理都在描述含着少量水的组织。

branches.en: DAMP MEDIA: soil and air hold water invisibly, one for roots and one as vapour.
branches.cn: 潮湿介质：土壤与空气都看不见地含水，一个为根系，一个以水汽。

branches.en: WATER AS A MEDIUM: in baking it keeps food soft; in cooking it carries heat as steam.
branches.cn: 水作介质：烘焙时它让食物柔软；烹饪时它以蒸汽搬运热量。

branches.en: EMOTION: tears rising make the eye itself the moist surface.
branches.cn: 情感：涌起的泪水让眼睛本身成了那块湿润的表面。

branches.en: PLACE: lasting dampness becomes a climate, no longer a passing sensation.
branches.cn: 地方：持久的潮湿变成一种气候，而不再是暂时的感觉。

intro.en: Moist is the base adjective of a productive family: -en makes a verb, -ness a quality noun, -ure a mass noun, and -ize builds the cosmetics verb.
intro.cn: moist 是一个能产词族的基础形容词：-en 造动词，-ness 造性质名词，-ure 造物质名词，-ize 造护肤动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin background of moist is disputed and cannot be stated safely, so the Latin entry list is empty on purpose. The related words below are all English formations or Old French borrowings.
latinIntro.cn: moist 的拉丁背景存在争议，无法稳妥陈述，因此拉丁词条列表按设计留空。下面的相关词都是英语构词或古法语借词。

items.meaningCN: 使微湿；沾湿（-en 表示「使……」）
items.example: Moisten the edge before sealing the envelope.
items.exampleCN: 封信封前先把边缘弄湿。

items.meaning: the state of being slightly wet
items.meaningCN: 湿润的状态（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The moistness of the air warned of rain.
items.exampleCN: 空气的湿润预示着要下雨。

items.meaningCN: 湿气；水分（-ure 构成物质名词）
items.example: The soil loses moisture in July.
items.exampleCN: 七月里土壤会失去水分。

items.meaning: to add water to skin or hair
items.meaningCN: 给皮肤或头发补水（-ize 构成动词）

items.meaning: a product used to add water to the skin
items.meaningCN: 保湿产品（-er 表示施动者）
items.example: She keeps a moisturizer in her bag.
items.exampleCN: 她包里常备一支保湿霜。

items.example: Store the salt in a moisture-proof jar.

items.meaning: heat carried by steam or water in cooking
items.meaningCN: 湿热（烹饪中由蒸汽或水传导的热）
items.exampleCN: 湿热做法能让肉保持嫩。

items.meaningCN: 眼含泪水的（moist 与 eyed 构成的复合形容词）
items.example: The audience sat moist-eyed at the end.
items.exampleCN: 结束时观众坐着，眼里含着泪。

definition_zh: 湿气；水分；潮气；含水量
definition_en: small amounts of water held on a surface, in the air, in soil or inside a material
core_image: 清晨的岩壁上凝着一层看不见的水汽，手指摸上去凉而微湿
scene: 清晨的岩壁上蒙着一层细水汽，摸上去凉凉的。Dew had left a thin film of moisture on the rock face.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「物体表面少量附着的水分」（第 1 个义项：表面的一层薄水）；句意为露水在岩壁上留下了一层薄薄的水汽；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 湿气；水分；潮气；含水量

senses.title: A thin film of water on a surface
senses.titleCN: 物体表面附着的一层薄水
senses.definition: a small amount of water lying on the surface of an object
senses.definitionCN: 附着在物体表面的一层少量水
senses.example: Dew had left a thin film of moisture on the rock face.
senses.exampleCN: 露水在岩壁上留下了一层薄薄的水汽。
senses.why: Moisture never names a body of water; it names water only as something small, held by a surface and waiting to evaporate.
senses.whyCN: moisture 从不指一片水域，只指被表面挽留、随时会蒸发掉的一点点水。

senses.title: Water vapour held in the air
senses.definition: water in the form of vapour that is present in the atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 以水汽形式存在大气中的水分
senses.example: The air in the greenhouse keeps enough moisture for the seedlings.
senses.exampleCN: 温室里的空气保持了足够幼苗生长的水汽。
senses.why: Air can hold water invisibly; when people speak of moisture in the air they mean this invisible load, not rain.
senses.whyCN: 空气能看不见地含水；说空气中的 moisture，指的是这份看不见的含水，而不是下雨。

senses.title: Water stored in soil
senses.definition: water held between soil particles and available to plant roots
senses.definitionCN: 保存在土壤颗粒之间、可供根系利用的水
senses.example: Mulch holds moisture in the soil through the dry months.
senses.exampleCN: 覆盖物在干旱的月份里把水分留在土壤中。
senses.why: Soil is another surface that can hold small amounts of water, so the same word extends from rock to earth.
senses.whyCN: 土壤也是能挽留少量水的表面，于是同一个词从岩石延伸到土地。

senses.title: Water content of food or material
senses.titleCN: 食物或材料内部的含水量
senses.definition: the water contained inside a substance such as grain, wood or plaster
senses.definitionCN: 谷物、木材、灰泥等物质内部所含的水
senses.example: The mill checks the moisture of every sack of grain before milling.
senses.exampleCN: 磨坊在研磨前检查每一袋谷物的含水量。
senses.why: Here the water is inside, not on the surface, but it is still a measured quantity that the material holds.
senses.whyCN: 这里的水在内部而不在表面，但仍然是材料所持有、可被计量的一份水。

senses.title: Water kept in living skin
senses.definition: the water naturally held in skin or hair, often spoken of in cosmetics
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤或头发中天然保持的水，常见于护肤语境
senses.example: This cream seals moisture into dry skin.
senses.exampleCN: 这款乳霜把水分锁在干燥的皮肤里。
senses.why: Living tissue is a moist surface, so its water became the standard subject of the word in skin-care writing.
senses.whyCN: 活体组织本身就是湿润的表面，因此护肤写作把皮肤里的水当成了这个词的固定对象。

senses.title: Condensation on a cold surface
senses.titleCN: 遇冷凝结在表面上的水
senses.definition: droplets that form when warm damp air meets a cold surface
senses.definitionCN: 暖湿空气遇到冷表面时凝结成的小水珠
senses.example: Moisture ran down the window in the warm kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 温暖的厨房里，水汽顺着窗玻璃往下流。
senses.why: This is the surface film again, but now produced by a temperature difference rather than by dew.
senses.whyCN: 这仍是表面那层水膜，只是成因从露水变成了温差。

senses.title: A measured water ratio
senses.titleCN: 作为仪器读数的含水率
senses.definition: the percentage of water in a material, measured for engineering or trade
senses.definitionCN: 为工程或交易测定出的材料含水百分比
senses.example: Engineers record the moisture content of the concrete before pouring.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在浇筑前记录混凝土的含水率。
senses.why: Once a value can be weighed and printed, the word turns into a number on a gauge.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这份水能被称量、打印出来，这个词就变成了仪表上的一个数字。

senses.title: Dampness as a building problem
senses.titleCN: 建筑中造成损坏的潮气
senses.definition: unwanted water inside walls or floors that damages a building
senses.definitionCN: 侵入墙体或地板、造成损坏的多余水分
senses.example: Moisture in the walls had softened the old plaster.
senses.exampleCN: 墙里的潮气早把旧灰泥泡软了。
senses.why: The same water that keeps a plant alive ruins plaster; when the holder is a building, the word turns into a fault.
senses.whyCN: 同一份水能养活植物，也能毁掉灰泥；当持有者是房屋时，这个词就变成了一个毛病。

intro.en: The word reached English through Old French, and its deeper Latin source is disputed. Dates are approximate and the contested step is marked.
intro.cn: 这个词经古法语进入英语，更早的拉丁来源存在争议。年代为大致估计，存疑的一环已明确标注。

items.en: Old French moistour 'moisture, dampness' was formed from moiste 'moist, wet' plus the noun suffix -our, from Latin -ura.
items.cn: 古法语 moistour「湿气、潮湿」由 moiste「湿的」加名词后缀 -our（出自拉丁 -ura）构成。

items.en: English borrowed the noun as moisture and used it first for dampness in air, soil and stored goods.
items.cn: 英语借入为 moisture，最早用于空气、土壤和储存货物中的潮气。

items.en: The adjective behind moist is usually reconstructed as Vulgar Latin *muscidus 'mouldy', an altered form of Latin mucidus. This reconstruction is a hypothesis, not a recorded form.
items.cn: moist 背后的形容词通常被重构为俗拉丁语 *muscidus「发霉的」，是拉丁语 mucidus 的变形。这一重构只是假说，并非有记录的形式。

items.en: Some scholars instead connect the Romance words to Latin madere 'to be wet' and madidus 'wet'. The two explanations are usually listed side by side; the source of moist is marked as source uncertain.
items.cn: 也有学者把这一组罗曼语词联系到拉丁语 madere「潮湿」和 madidus「湿的」。两种解释通常并列，moist 的来源不确定。

items.en: With the growth of agriculture, food processing and engineering, moisture came to mean a measurable water content rather than only a feeling of dampness.
items.cn: 随着农业、食品加工和工程的发展，moisture 逐渐指可测量的含水量，而不只是潮湿的感觉。

note.en: Group one holds forms that look or sound close to moisture; group two holds words that also name water held somewhere.
note.cn: 第一组是与 moisture 字形或读音接近的词；第二组是也指「某处所含的水」的词。

entries.definition: The comparative of the adjective moist, meaning more damp. It belongs to the same family and adds -er, not -ure.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词 moist 的比较级，表示更湿润。它属同一词族，词尾是 -er 而不是 -ure。

entries.definition: A combination of two or more substances. The middle consonant is -xt-, and the word comes from Latin miscere 'to mix', not from moist.
entries.definitionCN: 两种或多种物质的混合物。中间是 -xt-，源自拉丁语 miscere「混合」，与 moist 无关。

entries.definition: A cream that adds water to the skin; it is moisture plus -ize plus -er, so the ending is long and the meaning is a product.
entries.definitionCN: 给皮肤补水的乳霜；由 moisture 加 -ize 再加 -er 构成，词尾更长，指的是产品。

entries.definition: A mildly unpleasant wetness in air or in a material; it often carries a hint of discomfort that moisture does not.
entries.definitionCN: 空气或材料中令人略感不适的微湿；常带 moisture 所没有的不适意味。

entries.definition: The amount of water vapour in the air, usually reported as a percentage; it is the technical measure of atmospheric moisture.
entries.definitionCN: 空气中的水汽量，通常以百分比报告，是大气水分的技术指标。

entries.definition: The process by which vapour turns into liquid, or the drops produced; moisture on a window is its visible result.
entries.definitionCN: 水汽变成液体的过程，或由此产生的水珠；窗上的水汽就是它的可见结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes and real compounds, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：使用真实的后缀与真实的复合词，不编造顺口溜。

normal.en: moist + -ure: -ure is a noun suffix seen in pressure and departure, so the adjective 'wet' becomes the noun 'wetness'.
normal.cn: moist + -ure：-ure 是名词后缀（如 pressure、departure），于是形容词「湿的」变成名词「湿气」。

normal.en: moisten = moist + -en, the suffix that turns adjectives into verbs of making, as in widen and deepen.
normal.cn: moisten = moist + -en，这个后缀把形容词变成「使……」的动词，如 widen、deepen。

normal.en: moisturize = moisture + -ize, 'to put moisture into', and a moisturizer is the thing that does it.
normal.cn: moisturize = moisture + -ize，意为「把水分放进去」；moisturizer 就是做这件事的东西。

normal.en: moisture-proof = moisture + -proof 'resistant to', the same pattern as waterproof and fireproof.
normal.cn: moisture-proof = moisture + -proof「防……的」，与 waterproof、fireproof 同构。

normal.en: The fixed phrases soil moisture and moisture content turn invisible water into something a farmer or engineer can measure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配 soil moisture 与 moisture content 把看不见的水变成农民或工程师可以测量的东西。

abstract.en: Abstractly, moisture is water that has stopped moving: no river, no wave, only a film clinging to a surface. Symbol: a grey stone with one shining skin.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，moisture 是停止流动的水：不是河，不是浪，只是贴在表面上的一层膜。符号：一块灰石头上裹着一层发亮的薄皮。

abstract.en: The same film can live in air, in earth, in wood or in skin; the holder changes, the amount stays small.
abstract.cn: 同一层膜可以住在空气、泥土、木头或皮肤里；容器在变，量始终很小。

abstract.en: So moisture is not 'water' but 'water held'; the word always asks where it is kept and how much remains.
abstract.cn: 所以 moisture 不是「水」，而是「被留住的水」；这个词总在追问：它被存在哪里，还剩多少。

examples.en: A sealed jar keeps the moisture in the tobacco from escaping.
examples.cn: 密封的罐子能防止烟草里的水分跑掉。

examples.en: Farmers dig shallow pits to trap moisture during the dry season.
examples.cn: 农民在旱季挖浅坑来留住水分。

examples.en: The forecast warns that moisture from the gulf will bring heavy rain.
examples.cn: 预报提醒来自墨西哥湾的水汽将带来大雨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「抹湿的」：抹一下，表面就湿了 → moisture 湿气、水分

root: 古法语 moistour「湿气」← moiste「湿的」；再往前通常重构为俗拉丁语 *muscidus「发霉的」，也有人联系拉丁语 madere「潮湿」，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one idea: a small amount of water held by something. It starts on a surface, moves into air and soil, enters materials and skin, appears as condensation, becomes a measured ratio, and finally counts as damage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个意思展开：被某物留住的一点点水。它从表面开始，进入空气与土壤，进入材料与皮肤，又以凝结水的形态出现，随后变成可测的比值，最后被视为一种损坏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a little water that cannot flow away because a surface or a body holds it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一点无法流走的水，因为某个表面或物体把它留住了。

branches.en: VISIBLE FILM: dew on rock and condensation on glass are the same skin of water, produced by two different causes.
branches.cn: 可见水膜：岩石上的露与玻璃上的凝结水是同一层水皮，只是成因不同。

branches.en: HIDDEN HOLDERS: air and soil carry water without showing it, one as vapour and one between particles.
branches.cn: 隐形容器：空气与土壤都不显形地带着水，一个以水汽，一个在颗粒之间。

branches.en: INSIDE A SUBSTANCE: grain and concrete hold water that trade and engineering want as a number.
branches.cn: 物质内部：谷物与混凝土所含的水，是交易与工程想要的一个数字。

branches.en: LIVING TISSUE: skin and hair hold water that cosmetics try to keep in place.
branches.cn: 活体组织：皮肤与头发所含的水，是护肤品想留住的东西。

branches.en: FAULT: the same water becomes a defect when the holder is a wall or a floor.
branches.cn: 毛病：当容器是墙或地板时，同一份水就成了缺陷。

intro.en: Moisture sits at the centre of a small family of suffixes: -ure makes the noun, -en and -ize make verbs, -ness makes a quality, and -proof makes a defence.
intro.cn: moisture 处在一个小词族的中心：-ure 造名词，-en 与 -ize 造动词，-ness 造性质名词，-proof 造防护形容词。

latinIntro.en: Moist and moisture came through Old French, and the Latin step behind them is disputed. Because no Latin source can be stated safely, the Latin entry list is left empty on purpose.
latinIntro.cn: moist 与 moisture 经古法语而来，其背后的拉丁环节存在争议。由于无法稳妥地给出拉丁来源，拉丁词条列表按设计留空。

items.meaning: made so that damp cannot get in or out
items.example: The seeds are packed in moisture-proof foil.
items.exampleCN: 种子被装在防潮的铝箔袋里。

items.meaning: able to pull sweat or water away from a surface
items.meaningCN: 吸湿排汗的（wick 指把液体吸走）
items.exampleCN: 跑者更爱穿吸湿排汗的袜子。

items.meaning: to add water to the skin or hair
items.meaningCN: 给皮肤或头发补水（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: She moisturizes her hands after every wash.
items.exampleCN: 她每次洗手后都会给手补水。

items.meaning: a product that adds water to the skin
items.meaningCN: 保湿霜；润肤品（-er 表示做该动作的东西）
items.example: Use a light moisturizer under sunscreen.
items.exampleCN: 防晒霜下面先涂一层清爽的保湿霜。

items.meaningCN: 使微湿；沾湿（-en 表示「使……」）
items.example: Moisten the clay before you shape it.
items.exampleCN: 塑形之前先把黏土弄湿。

items.meaning: the quality of being slightly wet
items.meaningCN: 湿润；潮湿（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The moistness of the cake depends on the flour.
items.exampleCN: 蛋糕的湿润程度取决于面粉。

items.meaning: slightly wet, often in a pleasant way
items.meaningCN: 微湿的（常带宜人的意味），是本词族的基础形容词
items.example: The cake stays moist for three days.
items.exampleCN: 这块蛋糕能保持湿润三天。

items.meaning: water held in the ground, studied in farming and hydrology
items.meaningCN: 土壤水分（soil 与 moisture 构成的复合术语）
items.example: Sensors log soil moisture every hour.
items.exampleCN: 传感器每小时记录一次土壤水分。

definition_zh: 模具；霉；塑造；使成形
definition_en: a hollow container used to give shape to soft material; a growth of fungus on food or surfaces; to press material into a shape, or to influence how a person develops
core_image: 湿泥被按进木框，倒扣出来就是一只碗的形状
scene: 陶艺课上，师傅把湿泥按进木框里，再倒扣在架上，一排碗的雏形就出来了。She pressed the clay into a wooden mold and left it to dry.
sceneCN: 这里 mold 是「模具、模子」（第 1 个义项：让软材料成形的凹型容器）；句意为她把陶土按进木模具，然后放在一旁晾干。画面里能想见：木框、湿泥、倒扣出来的碗坯。

pos.zh: 模具；模子；霉；霉菌
塑造；使成形；用模具制作；影响（性格）

derivatives.zh: 由 mold 加 -ing 构成，义为「模制品；建筑上的线脚」
由 mold 加 -y 构成，义为「发霉的；有霉味的」
由 mold 加 -able 构成，义为「可塑的；容易成形的」
由 mold 加 -er 构成，义为「制模工」

senses.title: A hollow container that gives shape to soft material
senses.definition: a hollow container with a particular shape, into which soft material is pressed so that it takes that shape
senses.definitionCN: 具有特定形状的空心容器，把软材料压进去，材料就随之成型
senses.example: She pressed the clay into a wooden mold and left it to dry.
senses.exampleCN: 她把陶土按进木模具，然后放在一旁晾干。
senses.why: Latin modulus meant a small measure, and a mould is exactly a measured cavity: the size of the object is fixed before the material arrives.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 modulus 意为「小尺度」，而模子正是一个量好的空腔：材料还没进去，成品的尺寸就已经定死了。

senses.title: A growth of fungus on food or damp surfaces
senses.definition: a soft green, grey or white fungus that grows on food or on damp walls and leather
senses.definitionCN: 长在食物、潮湿墙面或皮革上的灰绿、灰白软质真菌
senses.example: There was black mold along the bathroom tiles.
senses.exampleCN: 浴室瓷砖的缝隙里长着黑霉。
senses.why: This sense is a different word in origin; it is usually linked to an old word for loose earth, because mould grows where things sit damp and begin to break down.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项在词源上是另一个词，一般认为与表示「松软泥土」的古词有关，因为霉总是长在潮湿、开始腐烂的东西上。

senses.title: To press material into a shape
senses.definition: to press a soft substance into a particular shape, by hand or with a container
senses.definitionCN: 用手或容器把柔软的物质压成某个形状
senses.example: He molded the wet sand into a small castle.
senses.exampleCN: 他把湿沙子塑成一座小城堡。
senses.why: If the mould is the measured cavity, the verb is the act of filling it; the word shifts from the tool to the work done with the tool.
senses.whyCN: 如果模子是量好的空腔，动词就是往里填的动作；词于是从工具转到用工具做的那件事。

senses.title: To shape a person's character or ideas
senses.definition: to influence strongly how someone's character, beliefs or habits develop
senses.definitionCN: 强烈影响某人的性格、信念或习惯如何发展
senses.example: School molded her into a careful reader.
senses.exampleCN: 学校把她培养成了一个细心的读书人。
senses.why: A child is soft material in the hands of family and teachers, so the same verb for pressing clay into a mould is used for forming a mind.
senses.whyCN: 孩子在家和老师手里就是软的材料，于是那个「把泥按进模子」的动词被借来形容心智的形成。

intro.en: Mold has two histories: the shaping word runs back to a Latin measure, while the fungus word is usually traced to an old word for earth.
intro.cn: mold 有两段来历：表示「成形」的那个词可追到拉丁语的尺度，表示「霉」的那个词一般认为来自表示泥土的古词。

items.en: Modulus was a small measure, a diminutive of modus, and it named the fixed size against which things were checked.
items.cn: modulus 是「小尺度」，由 modus 缩成，指用来核对事物的既定尺寸。

items.en: Old French modle took the word as a pattern or model, the shape a finished object should follow.
items.cn: 古法语把词写作 modle，指样板或模型，即成品应当照着做的形状。

items.en: Middle English used mold for the hollow pattern that potters and metal workers filled with their material.
items.cn: 中古英语用 mold 指陶工与金属工匠往里填料的空心模范。

items.en: The fungus sense is generally connected with Old English molde, loose earth; its exact development is uncertain, and dictionaries treat it as a separate word.
items.cn: 霉的义项一般认为与古英语 molde（松软泥土）有关，其确切演变不确定，词典把它当作另一个词处理。

items.en: Modern English keeps both senses in one spelling mold in American use, while British use writes mould; the extra u is usually explained as a later spelling habit.
items.cn: 现代英语在美式拼写里把两个义项都写成 mold，英式写 mould；多出来的 u 一般被解释为后来的拼写习惯。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers spellings and relatives built on the shaping word; the near-meaning group gathers words for casting, forming and fungus growth.
note.cn: 形近组收「成形」这个词上的拼写与同族词；近义组收表示浇铸、成形与霉菌生长的词。

entries.definition: The British spelling of mold, used for both the container and the fungus.
entries.definitionCN: mold 的英式拼写，模具与霉两个义项都用它。

entries.definition: Something made in a mold, or a shaped strip along a wall.
entries.definitionCN: 模制出来的东西，或墙面上的线脚。

entries.definition: Covered with or tasting of mold.
entries.definitionCN: 长满霉的；带着霉味的。

entries.definition: Soft enough to be pressed into a shape.
entries.definitionCN: 软到可以被压成形的；可塑的。

entries.definition: A small measure in Latin, the source of mold and of module.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中的「小尺度」，是 mold 与 module 的来源。

entries.definition: To pour melted metal or other material into a mold.
entries.definitionCN: 把熔化的金属等材料浇进模子。

entries.definition: To give something a particular form.
entries.definitionCN: 给某物一个特定的形状。

entries.definition: To make or develop into a particular shape or arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 使成为或发展成某种形状、结构。

entries.definition: A plant-like growth such as mold, mildew or mushroom.
entries.definitionCN: 霉、白粉病或蘑菇一类近似植物的生长物。

normalIntro.en: One spelling carries a family about measured cavities and a separate word about damp growth; both are worth keeping apart in memory.
normalIntro.cn: 同一个拼写承载着「量好的空腔」这一词族，也承载着另一个表示潮湿生长的词；记忆时要把两者分开。

normal.en: Modulus is Latin for a small measure, so a mold is a cavity whose size was decided in advance.
normal.cn: modulus 是拉丁语的「小尺度」，所以模子就是尺寸事先定好的空腔。

normal.en: Molding adds -ing: the thing that comes out of the mold, or the shaped strip on a wall.
normal.cn: molding 加 -ing：从模子里出来的东西，或墙上成形的线脚。
