normal.en: Moldy adds -y: full of mold, therefore spoiled and smelling of damp.
normal.cn: moldy 加 -y：长满霉，因此坏了、带着潮味。

normal.en: Moldable adds -able: able to take a shape, the way wet clay can.
normal.cn: moldable 加 -able：能够被塑成形状，就像湿陶土那样。

normal.en: British mould and American mold differ only in the u, as with colour and color.
normal.cn: 英式 mould 与美式 mold 只差一个 u，和 colour 与 color 的情况一样。

abstract.en: A mold is a promise made before the material arrives: the outcome is already written in the cavity.
abstract.cn: 模子是材料到来之前就许下的承诺：结果已经写在空腔里。

abstract.en: Shaping a child and shaping clay use one verb because both require gentle, repeated pressure.
abstract.cn: 塑造孩子与塑造陶土共用一个动词，因为两者都需要温和而反复的按压。

abstract.en: Mold the fungus is a reminder that soft, damp places quietly rewrite whatever rests in them.
abstract.cn: 表示霉的 mold 提醒人：柔软潮湿的地方会悄悄改写停放在那里的东西。

examples.en: She pressed the clay into a wooden mold and left it to dry.
examples.cn: 她把陶土按进木模具，然后放在一旁晾干。

examples.en: There was black mold along the bathroom tiles.
examples.cn: 浴室瓷砖的缝隙里长着黑霉。

examples.en: School molded her into a careful reader.
examples.cn: 学校把她培养成了一个细心的读书人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摸的」——用手摸摸湿泥，再按进框里；mold 就是模子、塑形。

root: 表示「成形」的 mold 来自拉丁语 modulus（小尺度，modus 的指小形式），经古法语 modle 进入英语；表示「霉」的义项一般认为另出自古英语 molde（泥土），来源不完全确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a measured hollow that decides a shape; from it come the container, the act of pressing, and the shaping of a mind, while the fungus sense is a separate old word that shares the spelling.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个决定形状的量好空腔；由此分出容器、按压动作与心智的塑造，而表示霉的义项是共用拼写的另一个古词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wet clay pressed into a wooden frame and turned out as a bowl.
core.cn: 核心意象：湿泥被按进木框，倒扣出来就是一只碗。

branches.en: rows of wooden frames waiting for clay
branches.cn: 一排等着装泥的木框

branches.en: a green patch spreading over old bread
branches.cn: 旧面包上蔓延的绿斑

branches.en: a hand pressing sand into a castle
branches.cn: 一只手把沙子压成城堡

branches.en: a teacher steadying a child's reading habit
branches.cn: 老师一点点扶正孩子的读书习惯

branches.en: a metal spoon lifted out of a sand mold
branches.cn: 从砂模里取出的金属勺

intro.en: A Latin measure word, its diminutive, a French pattern word and English endings from -ing to im- hold the shaping family together; the fungus sense sits outside it.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语尺度词、它的指小形式、一个法语「样板」词，加上从 -ing 到 im- 的英语词尾，撑起了「成形」这一族；表示霉的义项在这一族之外。

latinIntro.en: Modus and its diminutive modulus belong to the Latin vocabulary of measuring; the fungus sense has no Latin cognate and is left out of this list.
latinIntro.cn: modus 及其指小形式 modulus 属于拉丁语「量度」词汇；表示霉的义项没有拉丁同族词，因此不列入。

definition_zh: 分子；微粒；生物大分子；单分子；气体或液体中的独立单元；极少量；聚合物的重复单元；微小成分
definition_en: the smallest unit of a substance that keeps its chemical identity, consisting of two or more atoms held together by chemical bonds
core_image: 两个氧原子被一条看不见的弹簧拉住，独自成团地飘在空气里
scene: 两个氧原子被看不见的键牵在一起漂移，这样一个整体就是分子。Two oxygen atoms held together by an invisible bond drift as one group: that group is a molecule.
sceneCN: 这里 molecule 是「分子」（第 1 个义项：化学中的最小独立单元）；句意：两个氧原子被一条看不见的键拉在一起，作为一个整体在空气中漂移，这个整体就是分子。图中可辨识物件：两个相连的氧原子模型、代表化学键的虚线、空气背景中的其它分子、比例标尺；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 分子；微粒；极小量

forms.label: 名词（分子性；反应分子数）

senses.title: The chemical unit: atoms bonded into one group
senses.titleCN: 化学分子：原子成键组成的整体
senses.definition: the smallest unit of a substance that keeps its chemical identity, made of atoms held together by chemical bonds
senses.definitionCN: 保持物质化学性质的最小单元，由化学键连接的原子组成
senses.example: A water molecule contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
senses.exampleCN: 一个水分子含两个氢原子和一个氧原子。
senses.why: Molecule began as Latin molecula, 'a little mass'. Chemistry narrowed it to the smallest group of bonded atoms that still behaves as the substance, so the word moved from 'small lump' to 'bonded unit'.
senses.whyCN: molecule 最初是拉丁语 molecula「一小团物质」。化学把它收窄为仍然表现为该物质的最小成键原子团，于是词义从「小团块」转成「成键单元」。

senses.title: A tiny particle of matter
senses.definition: a very small particle of a substance, considered without regard to its internal bonds
senses.definitionCN: 物质中极小的颗粒，不考虑其内部成键情况
senses.example: Dust molecules coated the mirror.
senses.exampleCN: 灰尘微粒覆盖了镜面。
senses.why: The older, looser sense survives in ordinary speech, where any very small piece of matter may be called a molecule. Here the word means size, not chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 较旧、较松的义项在日常语言中留存，任何极小的物质碎屑都可能被称为 molecule。此处词义指的是大小，而不是化学。

senses.title: Biological macromolecule: proteins, DNA, starch
senses.titleCN: 生物大分子：蛋白质、DNA、淀粉
senses.definition: a very large molecule built from many repeating units, especially one found in living things
senses.definitionCN: 由许多重复单元构成的极大分子，尤指存在于生物体中的
senses.example: Each cell contains thousands of protein molecules.
senses.exampleCN: 每个细胞含有数千个蛋白质分子。
senses.why: Biology called its long chains molecules because they are bonded units, then added macro- when the size became the point. The base word keeps its chemical sense throughout.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把长链称为 molecule，因为它们就是成键单元；当大小成为重点时，又加上 macro-。词基本身始终保留化学义。

senses.title: Single-molecule work: studying one at a time
senses.titleCN: 单分子：一次只研究一个
senses.definition: in research, one individual molecule examined or manipulated on its own rather than in bulk
senses.definitionCN: 研究中指被单独观测或操作的那一个分子，而不是整批
senses.example: Single-molecule imaging revealed the folding steps.
senses.exampleCN: 单分子成像揭示了折叠的各个步骤。
senses.why: When instruments became sharp enough, the word needed a countable singular. Single-molecule marks the shift from averaging a crowd to watching one individual.
senses.whyCN: 当仪器足够精细时，这个词需要一个可数的单数形式。single-molecule 标记了从对一群分子取平均，转为观察单个分子的转变。

senses.title: The independent unit in a gas or liquid
senses.titleCN: 气体或液体中的独立单元
senses.definition: the separate unit that moves independently in a gas or solution, as opposed to a continuous network
senses.definitionCN: 在气体或溶液中独立运动的单元，与连续网络相对
senses.example: Gas molecules collide millions of times each second.
senses.exampleCN: 气体分子每秒碰撞数百万次。
senses.why: Kinetic theory needs a unit that travels freely. A molecule is exactly that: a bonded group small enough to move as one body through a fluid.
senses.whyCN: 动理论需要一个能自由行进的单元。分子正合适：那是一个小到能作为一个整体在流体中运动的成键原子团。

senses.title: A trace: a molecule of something
senses.definition: an extremely small amount of something, used in phrases such as not a molecule of truth
senses.definitionCN: 极少的量，用在 not a molecule of truth（一点真相也没有）一类的说法中
senses.example: There is not a molecule of evidence for that claim.
senses.exampleCN: 那个主张连一丝证据都没有。
senses.why: Because a molecule is invisibly small, the word can mean 'the least possible amount'. The metaphor borrows the chemist's smallest unit for the smallest imaginable trace.
senses.whyCN: 因为分子小到不可见，这个词可以表示「可能的最少量」。这一比喻借化学家的最小单位，指想象所及的最微小痕迹。

senses.title: The repeating unit of a polymer
senses.definition: in polymer chemistry, the repeating structural unit from which a long chain is built
senses.definitionCN: 高分子化学中指构成长链的重复结构单元
senses.example: Each molecule in the chain repeats the same pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 链中的每个单元重复着同一模式。
senses.why: Here the word names the brick rather than the wall. Polymer science counts how many molecule units are joined, so molecule marks the unit of repetition.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词指的是砖，而不是墙。高分子科学要数有多少个分子单元被连起来，因此 molecule 标记的是重复单位。

senses.title: A minute element of a larger thing
senses.titleCN: 微小成分：大事物里的一小点
senses.definition: a very small element or ingredient within a larger whole, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 较大整体中极小的成分或要素，用于比喻
senses.example: A molecule of doubt remained in his mind.
senses.exampleCN: 他心里还留着一丝疑虑。
senses.why: The figurative sense treats an idea as a substance with parts. One molecule of doubt is the smallest part that still counts as doubt, exactly as a molecule is the smallest part that still counts as the substance.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义把念头当作有组成部分的物质。一丝疑虑就是还算得上疑虑的最小部分，正如一个分子是还算得上该物质的最小部分。

intro.en: Molecule comes through French molécule from Latin molecula, a diminutive of moles 'mass, heap, massive structure'. The early sense was simply 'a small mass'. Modern chemistry fixed the meaning as a bonded group of atoms in the early 19th century, after Avogadro distinguished molecules from atoms. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: molecule 经法语 molécule 来自拉丁语 molecula，即 moles「块体、堆、庞大结构」的指小形式。早期义只是「一小团物质」。现代化学在 19 世纪初把词义固定为成键的原子团，此前阿伏伽德罗已区分分子与原子。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Chemistry fixes molecule as a bonded group of atoms, and single-molecule work appears much later with sharper instruments.
items.cn: 化学把 molecule 固定为成键的原子团；单分子研究则要晚得多，随着更精细的仪器才出现。

items.en: English molecule is borrowed in the general sense of a small mass or particle, before any chemical definition.
items.cn: 英语 molecule 在尚无化学定义时借入，泛指一小团物质或微粒。

items.en: French molécule is coined from the Latin diminutive as part of early corpuscular theory.
items.cn: 法语 molécule 由拉丁指小形式造出，属于早期微粒说的一部分。

items.en: molecula is moles 'mass' plus the diminutive -cula; it means a small mass, not a bonded group.
items.cn: molecula 是 moles「块体」加指小成分 -cula，意为小团物质，不是成键的原子团。

items.en: The origin of moles beyond Latin is of uncertain origin and is not securely tied to a reconstructed root.
items.cn: moles 在拉丁语之前的来源不确定，未能可靠地系于某个重构词根。

note.en: The first group separates three words that look related but are not, or are related only in one sense; the second compares units of matter at different levels.
note.cn: 第一组把三个看似相关、实则无关或只在某一义上相关的词分开；第二组比较不同层级上的物质单元。

entries.definition: a small burrowing animal. This word comes from Germanic roots and has no connection with molecula, despite the identical spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 一种小型穴居动物。这个词出自日耳曼词根，尽管拼写相同，却与 molecula 无关。

entries.definition: a small heap of earth thrown up by a burrowing mole. It belongs with the animal sense, not with the chemical unit.
entries.definitionCN: 鼹鼠刨出的小土堆，属于动物义那一支，与化学单位义无关。

entries.definition: a grinding tooth, from Latin mola 'millstone'. The chemistry adjective molar comes from mole instead, so the two meanings have different histories.
entries.definitionCN: 磨牙，出自拉丁语 mola「磨石」。化学形容词 molar 则出自 mole，两个含义历史不同。

entries.definition: the smallest unit of an element. Atoms are the parts that molecules are built from, so the two words mark different levels.
entries.definitionCN: 元素的最小单元。原子是构成分子的部件，因此两词标记不同层级。

entries.definition: a very small piece of matter. It says nothing about bonds, and may even be larger than a molecule.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的物质碎块。它不涉及成键，甚至可能比分子还大。

entries.definition: a substance made of two or more elements chemically joined. It names a material, while molecule names one unit of it.
entries.definitionCN: 由两种或以上元素化学结合而成的物质。它命名一种材料，而 molecule 命名该材料的一个单元。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pieces of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The -cule is a diminutive, so molecule literally begins as 'a small mass'.
normal.cn: -cule 是指小成分，所以 molecule 字面上起于「一小团物质」。

normal.en: Moles also gives demolish, 'to take the mass down', and mole as a breakwater, 'a mass built out'.
normal.cn: moles 还给出 demolish「把块体拆下」以及作防波堤解的 mole「向外筑起的块体」。

normal.en: The chemical unit and the unit of amount are linked: mole is simply molecule shortened.
normal.cn: 化学分子与物质的量单位是相连的：mole 就是 molecule 的缩略。

normal.en: The animal mole shares spelling but not history, so it never appears in chemistry.
normal.cn: 动物义的 mole 只是拼写相同，历史不同，因此从不进入化学语境。

normal.en: A molecule is the smallest piece that still behaves like the substance: split it and the substance is gone.
normal.cn: 分子是仍然表现得像该物质的最小部分：再切开，该物质就不存在了。

abstract.en: See two balls joined by a spring drifting as one body through empty space.
abstract.cn: 想象两个小球被一根弹簧连着，作为一个整体在空处漂移。

abstract.en: Every sense treats the molecule as a smallest whole: smallest unit, smallest particle, smallest trace, smallest ingredient.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都把分子当作一个最小的整体：最小单元、最小颗粒、最少痕迹、最小成分。

abstract.en: The word sits one floor above the atom and one floor below the material.
abstract.cn: 这个词位于原子之上、材料之下的一层。

examples.en: Ozone is a molecule of three oxygen atoms.
examples.cn: 臭氧是由三个氧原子构成的分子。

examples.en: The enzyme breaks each starch molecule into sugars.
examples.cn: 这种酶把每个淀粉分子分解成糖。

examples.en: Not a molecule of the original text survives.
examples.cn: 原文一丝一毫都没有留存下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫利Q」——莫利把Q弹的两个小球连成一小团，飘着走 → molecule 分子

root: 拉丁语 moles「块体、堆」＋指小成分 -cula → molecula「一小团物质」→ 法语 molécule → 英语 molecule。核心是「小到仍是该物质的最小一团」，化学把它定为成键的原子团。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one image: the smallest group that still counts as the thing. What changes is the frame — a chemical unit, a dust particle, a long biological chain, one observed individual, a free-flying gas unit, a trace, a repeating brick in a polymer, or a small ingredient of an idea.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个意象：仍然算得上「该物」的最小一团。变化的只是框架——化学单元、尘埃颗粒、生物长链、被观测的单个个体、自由飞行的气体单元、一丝痕迹、聚合物中的重复砖块，还是一个念头里的小成分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two oxygen atoms held by an invisible bond, drifting as one group.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个氧原子被看不见的键拉着，作为一个整体漂移。

branches.en: THE CHEMICAL UNIT: Latin 'small mass' becomes a bonded group, and long biological chains are still such groups.
branches.cn: 化学单元：拉丁语「小团」变成成键原子团，生物长链也仍是这样的原子团。

branches.en: MERE SIZE: in everyday use any very small particle may be called a molecule, with no chemistry implied.
branches.cn: 仅指大小：日常用法中任何极小的颗粒都可叫 molecule，不含化学意味。

branches.en: ONE UNIT VERSUS MANY: single-molecule work watches one, while kinetic theory treats each as a free traveller.
branches.cn: 一个与许多：单分子研究观察一个，动理论则把每个都当作自由行者。

branches.en: THE TRACE: the smallest imaginable amount borrows the chemist's smallest unit.
branches.cn: 痕迹：想象所及的最少量，借用了化学家的最小单位。

branches.en: THE BRICK AND THE INGREDIENT: polymers repeat one unit, and ideas are said to contain molecules of doubt.
branches.cn: 砖块与成分：聚合物重复同一单元，念头里则被说成含有「一丝」疑虑。

intro.en: Molecule is Latin molecula, a diminutive in -cula built on moles 'mass'. Its English relatives attach the suffixes -ar, -ity and the prefixes macro- and bi-.
intro.cn: molecule 是拉丁语 molecula，由 moles「块体」加指小成分 -cula 构成。它的英语同族词接上 -ar、-ity 后缀以及 macro-、bi- 前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pieces are moles 'mass, heap' and the diminutive -cula. moles also gives demolish and mole in the sense of a breakwater.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁成分是 moles「块体、堆」与指小成分 -cula。moles 还给出 demolish 以及作防波堤解的 mole。

items.meaningCN: 保持化学性质的最小单元
items.example: Each molecule of water is bent, not straight.
items.exampleCN: 每个水分子都是弯的，不是直的。

items.example: The two forms are molecularly identical.
items.exampleCN: 这两种形式在分子层面完全相同。

items.meaning: the number of molecules taking part in a reaction step
items.meaningCN: 一步反应中参与反应的分子数
items.example: A unimolecular step has molecularity one.
items.exampleCN: 单分子步骤的分子数为一。

items.example: Cellulose is a macromolecule of glucose units.
items.exampleCN: 纤维素是由葡萄糖单元构成的大分子。

items.example: Two moles of gas fill the flask.
items.exampleCN: 两摩尔气体充满这个烧瓶。

items.example: Molar mass is grams per mole.
items.exampleCN: 摩尔质量是每摩尔多少克。

items.structure: Latin moles for a great mass
items.meaning: a massive breakwater built into the sea

latinEntries.meaning: a mass, a heap, a massive structure

definition_zh: 片刻；时刻；时机；重要性
definition_en: a very short period of time; a particular point in time; the right point for doing something; formal importance or weight
core_image: 秒针刚跳过去一格，屋里恰好安静下来
scene: 锅里水刚开，母亲转身去接电话，回来时饺子已经全浮了起来。For a moment the kitchen was quiet enough to hear the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 moment 是「片刻、一会儿」（第 1 个义项：很短的一段时间）；句意为有短短一会儿，厨房安静得能听见雨声。画面里能想见：冒热气的锅、浮起的饺子、响起的电话。

pos.zh: 片刻；时刻；时机；重要性

collocations.zh: 关键时刻；见真章的一刻

derivatives.zh: 由 moment 加 -ary 构成，义为「瞬间的；短暂的」
由 momentary 加 -ly 构成，义为「片刻地；马上」
由 moment 加 -ous 构成，义为「重大的；影响深远的」
与 moment 同出拉丁语 momentum，义为「动量；势头」

senses.title: A very short period of time
senses.definition: a very short period of time, often shorter than a minute
senses.definitionCN: 很短的一段时间，常指不到一分钟
senses.example: For a moment the kitchen was quiet enough to hear the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 有短短一会儿，厨房安静得能听见雨声。
senses.why: Latin momentum first meant movement, and a moment is the smallest slice of movement you can notice, a tick of time that passes before anything else happens.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 momentum 起初表示「运动」，而 moment 就是你能察觉的最小一段运动：在别的事情发生之前先溜走的那一格时间。

senses.title: A particular point in time
senses.definition: a particular point in time, especially one that is remembered or waited for
senses.definitionCN: 某个特定的时间点，尤指被记住或等待的那一个
senses.example: The moment the lights went out, everyone froze.
senses.exampleCN: 灯灭的那一刻，所有人都僵住了。
senses.why: Once time is cut into ticks, one tick can be singled out and named; the word then stops being a length and becomes a marked position on the clock.
senses.whyCN: 时间一旦被切成格子，其中一格就能被单独挑出来命名；这个词于是不再表示长度，而表示钟面上的一个标记位置。

senses.title: The right point for doing something
senses.definition: the point at which something is best done, or when an important change becomes possible
senses.definitionCN: 最适合做某事的那个点，或重大变化可能发生的那个点
senses.example: The crisis became the moment for the old policy to end.
senses.exampleCN: 这场危机成了旧政策终止的时机。
senses.why: A single tick can carry a decision: when the word names one point, that point can also be the hinge on which later events turn.
senses.whyCN: 一格时间可以承载一个决定：当这个词指某一个点时，那个点也能成为后来事件转动所绕的轴。

senses.title: Importance or weight, in formal use
senses.definition: importance, especially in the phrase of great moment; a formal and rather old use
senses.definitionCN: 重要性，尤用于短语 of great moment；属正式而偏旧的用法
senses.example: The choice before the council was of great moment.
senses.exampleCN: 摆在议会面前的这个选择分量很重。
senses.why: Latin momentum also meant weight and influence, because something that moves carries force; English kept that sense for serious, formal matters.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 momentum 也指重量与影响力，因为运动的东西带着力量；英语把这个义项留给了严肃正式的场合。

intro.en: Moment is a contraction of a Latin word for movement, and its senses still follow the path from a moving body to a tick of time and to weight.
intro.cn: moment 是拉丁语表示「运动」的词缩合而来，它的义项仍沿着从运动之物到一格时间、再到分量的路线走。

items.en: Movere meant to move, and it supplied a large family of words about motion and change.
items.cn: movere 意为移动，派生出一整族与运动、变化有关的词。

items.en: Movimentum named a movement; in everyday speech the v dropped out and the word became momentum.
items.cn: movimentum 表示一次运动；在日常口语里 v 脱落，词形变成 momentum。

items.en: Momentum covered movement, the smallest division of time, and also weight or influence.
items.cn: momentum 兼指运动、最小的时间单位，以及重量或影响力。

items.en: Old French took the time sense as moment, meaning an instant, and passed it to English.
items.cn: 古法语取其中的时间义，写作 moment，意为瞬间，并传入英语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the short-time sense as the main one, adds the point-in-time and opportunity senses, and leaves importance to formal style.
items.cn: 现代英语以「短暂时间」为主体义项，又发展出时点与时机义，而「重要性」只留在正式文体里。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin movement root and its English family; the near-meaning group gathers words for instants, turning points and weight.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语「运动」词根及其英语词族展开；近义组收表示瞬间、转折点与分量的词。

entries.definition: Lasting only for an instant.
entries.definitionCN: 只持续一瞬的；短暂的。

entries.definition: For a very short time, or very soon.
entries.definitionCN: 片刻地；马上。

entries.definition: Of great importance, often because it changes a course of events.
entries.definitionCN: 重大的，常指会改变事态走向的。

entries.definition: The force of a moving body, or the push that keeps a process going.
entries.definitionCN: 运动物体的力；推动进程的势头。

entries.definition: An extremely short moment.
entries.definitionCN: 极短的一瞬。

entries.definition: A very short space of time, used loosely.
entries.definitionCN: 宽松说法中的一小会儿；分钟。

entries.definition: A particular point in time, especially one where decisions must be made.
entries.definitionCN: 特定时刻，尤指必须作决定的关头。

entries.definition: The importance or meaning that something carries.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物所具有的重要性或意义。

normalIntro.en: The word is a shrunk Latin movement word, and every sense is a different reading of what that small movement marks: a tick, a point, a hinge, a weight.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「运动」一词的缩形，每个义项都是对那一小段运动所标记之物的不同解读：一格、一点、一轴、一份重量。

normal.en: Movere is Latin for to move; drop the v from movimentum and momentum appears.
normal.cn: movere 是拉丁语的「移动」；把 movimentum 里的 v 去掉，就得到 momentum。

normal.en: The -ment in movement and the -ment of moment come from the same Latin habit of building nouns out of verbs.
normal.cn: movement 的 -ment 与 moment 的 -ment 源自同一个用动词造名词的拉丁习惯。

normal.en: Momentary adds -ary: lasting only a moment.
normal.cn: momentary 加 -ary：只持续一个片刻的。

normal.en: Momentous adds -ous: full of moment, therefore heavy with importance.
normal.cn: momentous 加 -ous：满是分量，因而是重大的。

normal.en: At the moment points to now; in a moment points to just after now.
normal.cn: at the moment 指向现在；in a moment 指向现在之后的一小会儿。

abstract.en: A moment is what a moving world leaves behind when you stop the film for one frame.
abstract.cn: moment 就是你按下暂停键时，这个运动的世界留下的那一帧画面。

abstract.en: Anything that moves carries weight, which is why the same word can mean both an instant and a serious matter.
abstract.cn: 凡是运动的东西都带着分量，所以同一个词既能指一瞬，也能指严肃大事。

abstract.en: A hinge is a small point that decides which way a large door swings.
abstract.cn: 合页是一个小点，却决定一扇大门往哪边开。

examples.en: For a moment the kitchen was quiet enough to hear the rain.
examples.cn: 有短短一会儿，厨房安静得能听见雨声。

examples.en: The moment the lights went out, everyone froze.
examples.cn: 灯灭的那一刻，所有人都僵住了。

examples.en: The choice before the council was of great moment.
examples.cn: 摆在议会面前的这个选择分量很重。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「默默」——沉默的一小会儿，就是片刻；moment 就是片刻、时刻。

root: 拉丁语 movere（移动）派生的 movimentum 缩合为 momentum（运动、瞬间、分量），经古法语 moment 进入英语；同族词多与运动、瞬间有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one tick of movement; the senses read that tick as a brief length, a marked point, a hinge for decisions and a measure of weight.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一格运动；义项把这一格读成一段短时长、一个标出的点、一处决策的轴心，以及一份分量的尺度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the second hand jumping one small step while the room falls silent.
core.cn: 核心意象：秒针刚跳过去一小格，屋里恰好安静下来。

branches.en: a kettle whistling, then silence for a breath
branches.cn: 水壶响过之后，静下一口气的工夫

branches.en: everyone looking up as the lights fail
branches.cn: 灯灭时所有人一起抬头

branches.en: a door left open at the exact second it matters
branches.cn: 在关键那一秒被推开的门

branches.en: a council raising a hand at the turning point
branches.cn: 转折点上举手的议事会

branches.en: a heavy file placed on a light table
branches.cn: 重文件压在轻桌子上

intro.en: A Latin verb of moving, its contracted noun, a French instant and four English endings turn a step of movement into time and importance.
intro.cn: 一个表示移动的拉丁动词、它缩合而成的名词、一个法语词和四个英语词尾，把一步运动变成了时间与分量。

latinIntro.en: Movere, movimentum and momentum are recorded Latin forms, and momentum is the direct source of the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: movere、movimentum 与 momentum 都是有记录的拉丁词形，其中 momentum 是英语名词的直接来源。

items.meaning: a brief time; a point in time
belonging to, of the nature of
result or means of an action
items.meaningCN: 名词后缀：动作的结果或手段

definition_zh: 钱；货币；财富；款项
definition_en: coins and notes used to buy things; wealth in general; funds collected or set aside for a purpose; the pay received for work
core_image: 铁盒里一叠皱巴巴的纸币，被手指一张张抹平
scene: 集市快收摊了，父亲把皱巴巴的纸币一张张抹平，再塞进旧铁盒。He counted the money twice before putting it in the tin.
sceneCN: 这里 money 是「钱、货币」（第 1 个义项：用来买东西的钱币）；句意为他把钱数了两遍，才放进铁盒。画面里能想见：收摊的集市、皱巴巴的纸币、旧铁盒。

pos.zh: 钱；货币；财富；款项

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 monet- 加 -ary 构成，义为「货币的；金融的」
由 monet- 加 -ize 构成，义为「使货币化；靠……赚钱」
由 money 加 -ed 构成，义为「有钱的」
由 money 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无钱的」

senses.title: Coins and notes used to buy things
senses.definition: the coins and notes that people use to buy and sell things
senses.definitionCN: 人们用来买卖东西的硬币与纸币
senses.example: He counted the money twice before putting it in the tin.
senses.exampleCN: 他把钱数了两遍，才放进铁盒。
senses.why: The Latin word moneta began as the name of the mint where Roman coins were struck, then slid from the place of making to the thing made.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 moneta 起初是罗马铸币厂的名字，后来从「制造的地点」滑到「造出来的东西」。

senses.title: Wealth in general
senses.definition: wealth considered as a whole, including property and savings as well as cash
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体看待的财富，除现金外还包括房产与积蓄
senses.example: The family lost all its money in the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 这场火让这家人失去了全部财产。
senses.why: Once a word means coins, it easily widens to everything those coins can buy, so money comes to stand for the whole pile rather than the pieces.
senses.whyCN: 一个词一旦指硬币，就很容易扩到这些硬币能买下的一切；于是 money 转而指整堆财富，而不是一枚枚硬币。

senses.title: Funds set aside for a purpose
senses.definition: money collected or kept for a particular aim, such as building a school or running a service
senses.definitionCN: 为某个特定目标筹集或留存的钱，如建校或维持服务
senses.example: The council put public money into the new library.
senses.exampleCN: 议会把公共资金投进了新图书馆。
senses.why: Money is countable in this sense as sums set apart: the word no longer asks what you own but what has been assigned to a job.
senses.whyCN: 在这个义项里，money 可以按「分拨出来的款项」计数：它问的不再是你有多少，而是哪一笔钱被派了什么用途。

senses.title: Pay received for work
senses.definition: the amount a person is paid for their work, often judged as good or bad
senses.definitionCN: 一个人工作所得的报酬，常以高低来评价
senses.example: The money is good, but the hours are long.
senses.exampleCN: 报酬不错，可是工时太长。
senses.why: When money is what a job hands over, the same word measures a wage, and the phrase the money is good simply reports that the pay is generous.
senses.whyCN: 当 money 指一份工作交到你手里的东西时，同一个词就在衡量工资；the money is good 这句话只是说明报酬丰厚。

intro.en: Money comes from a Latin name for a mint, which itself grew from a verb meaning to warn; the place of coin-making gave its name to the coins.
intro.cn: money 来自拉丁语中对铸币厂的称呼，而那个称呼又长自动词「警告」；造币之地把自己的名字给了造出来的钱。

items.en: Monere meant to warn or to advise, and it stands behind the epithet of Juno whose temple held the Roman mint.
items.cn: monere 意为警告、提醒，朱诺的称号就由它而来，而罗马铸币厂正设在朱诺神庙里。

items.en: Moneta first named the mint, the place where silver was struck into coin, and later the coin itself.
items.cn: moneta 先指铸币厂，即把白银打成硬币的地方，后来也指硬币本身。

items.en: A monetarius was an officer of the mint, and the adjective monetarius described anything belonging to coining.
items.cn: monetarius 是铸币厂的官吏，而同形的形容词表示「与铸币有关的」。

items.en: Old French moneie carried the coin sense and also the sense of coined wealth into everyday use.
items.cn: 古法语 moneie 把「硬币」义以及「由钱构成的财富」义带入日常使用。

items.en: Modern English money keeps the mass-noun sense, adds funds and pay, and allows the formal plural monies for separate sums.
items.cn: 现代英语的 money 保留不可数名词的用法，又添上「资金」与「报酬」，并允许用正式复数 monies 指分开的多笔款项。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin mint word and its English family; the near-meaning group gathers words for cash, circulating value and wealth.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语「铸币厂」一词及其英语词族展开；近义组收表示现金、流通价值与财富的词。

entries.definition: Connected with money or the currency of a country.
entries.definitionCN: 与货币或一国通货有关的。

entries.definition: To turn something into a source of money.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物变成赚钱的来源。

entries.definition: Rich, or coming from wealthy people.
entries.definitionCN: 有钱的，或来自富裕阶层的。

entries.definition: The place where a country makes its coins.
entries.definitionCN: 一国制造硬币的地方；铸币厂。

entries.definition: Coins and notes in hand, rather than money in an account.
entries.definitionCN: 手头的硬币和纸币，区别于账户里的钱。

entries.definition: The money a country uses and that is accepted in it.
entries.definitionCN: 一国使用并在该国通行的货币。

entries.definition: A large amount of money and property owned by someone.
entries.definitionCN: 某人拥有的大量钱财与财产。

entries.definition: Money available to be spent for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 可供用于某个目的的钱；资金。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as the name of a building where coins were made, and its family keeps returning to mints, currency and the wealth coins stand for.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起初是一处造币建筑的名字，词族反复回到铸币厂、通货，以及硬币所代表的财富。

normal.en: Moneta is Latin for a mint, so money first names the place where coin is made, then the coin that came out.
normal.cn: moneta 是拉丁语的「铸币厂」，所以 money 先指造币的地方，再指造出来的硬币。

normal.en: Monetary adds -ary to the stem monet-: anything belonging to money.
normal.cn: monetary 在词干 monet- 后加 -ary：属于货币的一切。

normal.en: Monetize adds -ize: to turn a thing into money or into a way of earning.
normal.cn: monetize 加 -ize：把某样东西变成钱或变成赚钱的方式。

normal.en: Moneyed adds -ed: supplied with money, therefore rich.
normal.cn: moneyed 加 -ed：有钱供着，因而是富有的。

normal.en: Money is usually uncountable, so we say much money or a sum of money, not a money.
normal.cn: money 通常不可数，所以说 much money 或 a sum of money，而不说 a money。

abstract.en: A mint is a room where metal is pressed into promises; the word carries that promise long after the building is gone.
abstract.cn: 铸币厂是把金属压成承诺的房间；建筑早已不在，这个词仍带着那份承诺。

abstract.en: The same word covers a coin, a fortune and a budget because all three are the same thing at different scales.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖一枚硬币、一笔家产和一份预算，因为这三者只是同一件东西的不同尺度。

abstract.en: Counting money twice is an old habit: value felt in the hand is heavier than value written in an account.
abstract.cn: 把钱数两遍是老习惯：握在手里的价值，比写在账上的价值更沉。

examples.en: He counted the money twice before putting it in the tin.
examples.cn: 他把钱数了两遍，才放进铁盒。

examples.en: The family lost all its money in the fire.
examples.cn: 这场火让这家人失去了全部财产。

examples.en: The council put public money into the new library.
examples.cn: 议会把公共资金投进了新图书馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马尼」——听着像马驮着的尼龙袋，里面装的全是钱；money 就是钱。

root: 拉丁语 moneta（罗马的铸币厂，设在朱诺神庙）经古法语 moneie 进入英语；同族词多与铸币、货币、财富有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is coin struck at a mint; the senses widen from coin to the whole of one's wealth, to funds tied to a purpose, and to the pay a job brings.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是在铸币厂打出的硬币；义项从硬币扩到全部家产、指定用途的资金，以及工作带来的报酬。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of crumpled notes being smoothed flat and tucked into a tin box.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠皱巴巴的纸币被抹平，塞进铁盒。

branches.en: a handful of coins pushed across a counter
branches.cn: 几枚硬币被推过柜台

branches.en: a tin box holding the savings of a whole family
branches.cn: 一只装着一家人积蓄的铁盒

branches.en: a house and a field counted as one estate
branches.cn: 把房子和田地算作同一份家产

branches.en: a labelled jar of funds for a new roof
branches.cn: 贴着标签、攒着修屋顶的资金罐

branches.en: a pay slip read twice at the kitchen table
branches.cn: 在厨房桌上看了两遍的工资单

intro.en: A Latin verb of warning, the mint it named, the officer of that mint and four English endings carry the word from a building to cash, wealth and pay.
intro.cn: 一个表示「警告」的拉丁动词、它命名的铸币厂、厂里的官吏，以及四个英语词尾，把这个词从一座建筑带到了现金、财富与报酬。

latinIntro.en: Monere, moneta and monetarius are recorded Latin forms; the mint word is the direct ancestor of the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: monere、moneta 与 monetarius 都是有记录的拉丁词形，其中表示铸币厂的那个词是英语名词的直接祖先。

definition_zh: 显示器；监测仪；班长；监督者；监测；监控；监听
definition_en: a device that displays or records information, a person who warns or keeps order, or to watch and check something continuously over time
core_image: 一个站在旁边不断提醒“注意”的人，眼睛一直盯着同一处
scene: 控制室里，工程师盯着显示管道压力的监视器。From the control room the engineer watched the monitor that showed the pressure inside the pipeline.
sceneCN: 这里 monitor 是「显示器」（第 1 个义项：显示画面或数据的屏幕）；句意：工程师在控制室里盯着显示管道内压力的显示器。场景要点：昏暗的控制室、一排亮着的屏幕、屏幕上跳动的压力曲线、管道剖面图；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 显示器；监测仪；班长；监督者；告诫者
监测；监控；监听；跟踪观察

senses.title: A screen that shows the picture
senses.definition: a screen, especially a computer or television display, that shows information or a picture
senses.definitionCN: 显示信息或画面的屏幕，尤指电脑或电视显示屏
senses.example: The second monitor shows the camera feed from the front door.
senses.exampleCN: 第二块显示器显示前门的摄像头画面。
senses.why: Broadcasting used a monitor for a device that continuously checked a transmission, and the screen showing that check took the name. A computer display repeats the role: it lets someone keep watch on what the machine is doing.
senses.whyCN: 广播业曾把持续检查传输质量的设备称为 monitor，显示这项检查的屏幕便沿用了这个名字。电脑显示器重复着同一角色：让人持续看清机器在做什么。

senses.title: An instrument that keeps watch
senses.definition: a device that continuously measures and displays a physical condition, such as heart rate or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 持续测量并显示某项身体或物理状况的设备，如心率或压力
senses.example: The heart monitor began to beep faster and faster.
senses.exampleCN: 心脏监测仪开始越响越快地鸣叫。
senses.why: The Latin monitor was a person who warned. An instrument that watches a pulse and sounds an alarm takes over the warning job, so the person's title passes to the machine.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 monitor 是一个发出警告的人。一台盯着脉搏、并发出警报的仪器接过了这份警告的职责，于是人的称呼转移到了机器上。

senses.title: The pupil who keeps order
senses.definition: a senior pupil at a school given the task of keeping order or checking attendance
senses.definitionCN: 学校里被赋予维持秩序或检查出勤任务的高年级学生
senses.example: The hall monitor checked the corridors every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 走廊值日生每小时巡查一次走廊。
senses.why: This is the oldest English sense, from 1540s: a senior pupil 'charged with keeping order'. The student does exactly what the Latin word says — reminds others of the rules and reports breaches.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语里最古老的义项，始于 16 世纪 40 年代：受命维持秩序的高年级学生。这个学生做的正是拉丁词所说的——提醒别人守规矩，并报告违规。

senses.title: An official who warns
senses.definition: a person appointed to observe, advise, and warn, especially in an official or technical role
senses.definitionCN: 受指派观察、建议并提出告诫的人，尤指担任正式或技术职务者
senses.example: A monitor was appointed to warn the committee about conflicts of interest.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会任命了一名监督员，就利益冲突提出告诫。
senses.why: Latin monitor meant 'one who reminds, admonishes, or checks', and also 'an overseer, instructor, guide'. The English noun keeps that advisory, warning figure before it ever names a machine.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 monitor 意为“提醒者、告诫者、检查者”，也指“监督者、指导者、引路人”。英语名词先保留了这个提出建议与警告的人，之后才用它命名机器。

senses.title: Watch the numbers over time
senses.definition: to measure and check a quantity or condition regularly over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内定期测量并检查某个数量或状况
senses.example: Sensors monitor the temperature of the tank every ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器每十分钟监测一次储罐的温度。
senses.why: The verb appeared in 1924 for checking the quality of radio signals. Its core is repetition: a monitor does not look once but keeps looking, so the verb means sustained checking rather than a single glance.
senses.whyCN: 动词于 1924 年出现，指检查无线电信号的质量。它的核心是重复：monitor 不是看一眼，而是持续地看，所以这个动词表示持续的检查，而不是一瞥。

senses.title: Keep someone under surveillance
senses.definition: to watch a person, group, or activity closely, especially to detect wrongdoing or risk
senses.definitionCN: 密切注视某人、某群体或某项活动，尤为了发现不当行为或风险
senses.example: The company monitors its drivers' speed and braking through an app.
senses.exampleCN: 公司通过一个应用监控司机的车速与刹车情况。
senses.why: When the watching is turned from a gauge to people, the warning role becomes surveillance. The same continuous attention is now aimed at behaviour that may need correcting.
senses.whyCN: 当注视的对象从仪表转向人，提醒的职责就变成了监控。同样的持续关注，现在对准了可能需要纠正的行为。

senses.title: Listen to a channel
senses.definition: to listen to a radio, telephone, or other channel continuously in order to catch particular information
senses.definitionCN: 持续收听无线电、电话或其他频道，以捕捉特定信息
senses.example: They monitored the radio channel all night, waiting for a reply.
senses.exampleCN: 他们整夜监听那个无线电频道，等待回复。
senses.why: The earliest verb sense was exactly this: checking radio signals for quality. Listening to a channel is watching with the ears, and the word's continuity remains.
senses.whyCN: 最早的动词义正是这个：检查无线电信号的质量。用耳朵听一个频道就是“用耳朵看”，而这个词的持续性仍然保留。

senses.title: The lizard that warns
senses.definition: a large lizard of the family Varanidae, called a monitor because of an old story that it warned people of crocodiles
senses.definitionCN: 巨蜥科的大型蜥蜴，因古老传说称它会向人预警鳄鱼而得名
senses.example: A monitor lizard crossed the trail and disappeared into the grass.
senses.exampleCN: 一只巨蜥穿过小径，消失在草丛里。
senses.why: The name was given in 1826 because the lizard was fabled to give warning of Nile crocodiles. It is the same 'warner' sense, applied to an animal rather than a person or device.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字始于 1826 年，因为传说这种蜥蜴会预警尼罗河鳄鱼。它仍是“警告者”这层意思，只是用在了动物身上，而不是人或设备。

senses.title: The ironclad that admonished
senses.definition: the name of the first ironclad warship of that design, built in 1862 and intended as a warning to the Confederacy
senses.definitionCN: 1862 年建造的第一艘该型铁甲舰的名称，意在向南方邦联发出警告
senses.example: The Monitor fought the Merrimack in 1862 and changed naval warfare.
senses.exampleCN: 1862 年，莫尼特号与梅里马克号交战，改变了海战方式。
senses.why: The inventor chose the name because the ship was meant to 'admonish' Confederate leaders. The Latin warner becomes a floating threat, a warning made of iron.
senses.whyCN: 发明者选择这个名字，是因为这艘船意在“告诫”南方邦联的领导人。拉丁语的告诫者变成了浮在水上的威胁，一个用铁铸成的警告。

senses.title: A background watcher in software
senses.titleCN: 软件中的后台监控程序
senses.definition: in computing, a program or process that runs in the background and checks system activity
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，指在后台运行、检查系统活动的程序或进程
senses.example: A background monitor logs every login and flags unusual hours.
senses.exampleCN: 一个后台监控程序记录每次登录，并标记异常时段。
senses.why: Software repeats the human watchman: it runs unnoticed, checks continuously, and reports what looks wrong. The old 'one who warns' is now a loop of code.
senses.whyCN: 软件重复着人类更夫的角色：它不声不响地运行，持续检查，并报告看起来不对的地方。古老的“告诫者”如今成了一段循环的代码。

intro.en: Monitor began as a Latin word for a person who warns, entered English in the sixteenth century as a school officer, and only in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries became a machine, a lizard, a warship, and finally a screen. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: monitor 最初是拉丁语中表示“告诫者”的词，16 世纪作为学校职务进入英语，直到 19 与 20 世纪才变成仪器、蜥蜴、军舰，最后成为屏幕。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'senior pupil at a school charged with keeping order'. It came from Latin monitor.
items.cn: 英语最早记录为“受命维持秩序的学校高年级学生”。它来自拉丁语 monitor。

items.en: Latin monitor meant 'one who reminds, admonishes, or checks', and also 'an overseer, instructor, guide, teacher'. It was an agent noun from monere.
items.cn: 拉丁语 monitor 意为“提醒者、告诫者、检查者”，也指“监督者、指导者、引路人、教师”。它是 monere 的施动名词。

items.en: Monere meant 'to remind, bring to one's recollection, tell of; admonish, advise, warn, instruct, teach'. It goes back to PIE *moneie-, a causative form of *men- 'to think', the root also behind Latin memini 'I remember' and mens 'mind'.
items.cn: monere 意为“提醒、使想起、告知；告诫、建议、警告、指导、教导”。它可追溯到原始印欧语 *moneie-，即 *men-“思考”的使役形式；同一词根也是拉丁语 memini“我记得”与 mens“心智”的来源。

items.en: The monitor lizard was so called because it was fabled to warn people of Nile crocodiles (1826). The ironclad warship Monitor (1862) was named by its inventor because it was meant to 'admonish' Confederate leaders.
items.cn: 巨蜥被称为 monitor，是因为传说它会向人预警尼罗河鳄鱼（1826）。铁甲舰莫尼特号（1862）由发明者命名，因为这艘船意在“告诫”南方邦联的领导人。

items.en: The verb is recorded in 1924 meaning 'to check for quality', originally of radio signals. The general sense 'observe, keep under review' is from 1944. Keats had used it in 1818 to mean 'to guide'.
items.cn: 动词于 1924 年有记录，意为“检查质量”，最初用于无线电信号。泛指“观察、持续审视”的义项始于 1944 年。济慈在 1818 年曾用它表示“引导”。

items.en: A broadcasting sense, 'a device to continuously check on the technical quality of a transmission', is recorded from 1931 and led to the sense 'a TV screen displaying the picture from a particular camera'. The computer display is a later extension of that screen sense.
items.cn: 广播义“持续检查传输技术质量的设备”记录于 1931 年，并由此引出“显示某一摄像机画面的电视屏幕”这一义项。电脑显示器是该屏幕义的后期引申。

note.en: The first group separates the noun and adjective forms built on monitor from two related warning words; the second compares the verbs of watching that learners use interchangeably.
note.cn: 第一组把由 monitor 构成的名词与形容词形式，同两个相关的“警告”词分开；第二组比较学习者常互换使用的几个“看管”动词。

entries.definition: the continuous act of checking or watching something. It is the process, while monitor is the device or the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 持续检查或观察的行为。它是过程，而 monitor 是设备或动词。

entries.definition: giving or serving as a warning. It keeps the Latin sense of admonition and is mostly formal.
entries.definitionCN: 给予警告的，或起警告作用的。它保留了拉丁语“告诫”的意思，多用于正式语境。

entries.definition: to warn or reprimand someone firmly but not harshly. It shares the Latin monere root but is a separate verb, not a form of monitor.
entries.definitionCN: 坚定但不严厉地警告或责备某人。它与 monitor 共享拉丁语 monere 词根，但它是另一个动词，不是 monitor 的词形。

entries.definition: a feeling that something is about to happen, especially something bad. It is a warning that comes before the event, built with pre- 'before'.
entries.definitionCN: 一种某事即将发生、尤指坏事的感觉。它是事件之前到来的警告，由 pre-“在前”构成。

entries.definition: to be in charge of people or work and make sure it is done properly. It stresses authority over workers, while monitor stresses continuous checking of signals or conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 负责管理人或工作，确保事情做好。它强调对工作者的权威，而 monitor 强调对信号或状况的持续检查。

entries.definition: to look at something for a period of time, often without measuring it. Monitor usually adds a purpose: to detect change, risk, or poor quality.
entries.definitionCN: 在一段时间内看着某物，通常不进行测量。monitor 通常多一层目的：发现变化、风险或质量问题。

entries.definition: to follow the movement or development of something over time, often by recorded traces. It focuses on where something goes; monitor focuses on whether it stays within limits.
entries.definitionCN: 随时间跟踪某物的移动或发展，常依据记录下来的痕迹。它关注东西去了哪里，monitor 关注它是否仍在限度之内。

entries.definition: to examine people, substances, or signals in order to sort or filter them. It is usually a test applied at a point in time, while monitor is a watch kept over time.
entries.definitionCN: 检查人、物质或信号，以便分类或筛选。它通常是在某一时点施行的检验，而 monitor 是长期保持的观察。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin monere 'warn', the agent noun monitor, and the English family monitoring, monitory, admonish, and premonition.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 monere“警告”、施动名词 monitor，以及英语词族 monitoring、monitory、admonish、premonition。

normal.en: monere means 'to warn, remind'. A monitor is literally 'one who warns' — first a pupil, then an instrument, then a screen.
normal.cn: monere 意为“警告、提醒”。monitor 字面上就是“发出警告的人”——先是学生，再是仪器，最后是屏幕。

normal.en: The school sense is the oldest English one (1540s); the machine and screen senses are centuries later.
normal.cn: 学校职务义是英语里最古老的义项（16 世纪 40 年代）；仪器与屏幕义要晚好几个世纪。

normal.en: The verb arrived in 1924 for checking radio signal quality, which is why 'monitor a channel' still sounds natural.
normal.cn: 动词于 1924 年出现，用于检查无线电信号质量，所以 monitor a channel 至今听起来自然。

normal.en: monitoring is the process, monitory is 'warning', admonish is a separate verb from the same root.
normal.cn: monitoring 是过程，monitory 是“警告的”，admonish 则是同根的另一动词。

normal.en: A monitor differs from a supervisor: it keeps checking a signal or condition, while a supervisor holds authority over people.
normal.cn: monitor 与 supervisor 不同：它持续检查信号或状况，而 supervisor 对人拥有管理权。

abstract.en: Picture a night watchman at a factory gate. He does not repair anything; he looks, checks, and raises the alarm.
abstract.cn: 想象一名守在工厂大门的更夫。他不修理任何东西；他看、检查、发出警报。

abstract.en: Move that watchman into a box on the wall, and he becomes a heart monitor; put his gaze on a screen, and he becomes a display.
abstract.cn: 把这位更夫装进墙上的盒子，他就成了心脏监测仪；把他的目光放到屏幕上，他就成了显示器。

abstract.en: The word always means attention spread over time: a single look is not monitoring, however careful it is.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终表示铺在时间上的注意：只看一眼，无论多仔细，都不算监测。

examples.en: Nurses monitor the patient's pulse and blood pressure every hour.
examples.cn: 护士每小时监测病人的脉搏与血压。

examples.en: The app monitors how much time you spend on each website.
examples.cn: 这个应用监控你在每个网站上花多少时间。

examples.en: The teacher left a monitor in charge of the class while she fetched the keys.
examples.cn: 老师去取钥匙时，让班长负责管班。

dict_mnemonic.text: “莫离他”——莫要离开他，他一直在旁边盯着、随时提醒你 → monitor 监视器；监测（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 monere“警告、提醒”的施动名词 monitor“告诫者”，核心是“持续盯着并随时发出提醒”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of monitor, all held together by one figure: someone standing beside a thing, watching without stopping and speaking up when something is wrong.
sensesIntro.cn: monitor 的十个义项都由同一个形象串起：有人站在某物旁边，不停地看，一有不对就出声提醒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warner standing beside, eyes fixed on one spot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个站在旁边、目光钉在一处的告诫者。

branches.en: INSTRUMENTS: the warner becomes a measuring device, and the screen that shows its check takes the same name.
branches.cn: 仪器：告诫者变成测量设备，显示这项检查的屏幕也沿用了同一个名字。

branches.en: PEOPLE: the oldest senses keep a person in the role, either a pupil keeping order or an official who warns.
branches.cn: 人：最古老的义项让一个人留在这个角色里，或是维持秩序的学生，或是提出告诫的官员。

branches.en: WATCHING: the verb checks quantities over time, and when aimed at people it becomes surveillance.
branches.cn: 注视：动词随时间检查数量，而当对象转向人时，它就变成监控。

branches.en: LISTENING: a channel is watched with the ears, the earliest verb use of all.
branches.cn: 监听：频道是用耳朵看的，这是所有动词用法中最早的一个。

branches.en: THE NAME TRAVELS: a lizard fabled to warn, an ironclad built to admonish, and a background program that keeps checking.
branches.cn: 名字远行：传说会预警的蜥蜴、为告诫而造的铁甲舰，以及持续检查的后台程序。

intro.en: Monitor is a Latin agent noun in -itor built on mon- 'warn'. English adds -ing, -y, -ial and -ship, while the same root also reaches English through admonish, monition, and premonition.
intro.cn: monitor 是拉丁语中以 -itor 结尾的施动名词，词干 mon- 意为“警告”。英语加上 -ing、-y、-ial 与 -ship，同一词根还通过 admonish、monition、premonition 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is monere 'warn, remind', its agent noun monitor, and the action noun monitio 'a warning'. Summon also belongs here: Latin summonere meant 'hint, remind, warn'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词族包括 monere“警告、提醒”、它的施动名词 monitor，以及行为名词 monitio“警告”。summon 也属于这里：拉丁语 summonere 意为“暗示、提醒、警告”。

items.meaning: one who warns or checks; a checking device
items.meaningCN: 告诫者；检查者；监测设备（mon- 警告 + -itor 施动名词）
items.example: The monitor on the wall showed a steady line.
items.exampleCN: 墙上的监测仪显示出一条平稳的线。

items.meaningCN: 监测；监控（-ing 构成过程名词）
items.example: The patient was kept under close monitoring.
items.exampleCN: 病人被置于密切监测之下。

items.meaningCN: 告诫的；警告的（-ory 构成形容词）
items.example: He gave a monitory glance at the noisy table.
items.exampleCN: 他朝吵闹的那桌投去一个警告的目光。

items.meaning: relating to a monitor or prefect
items.meaningCN: 级长的；监督的（-ial 构成形容词）
items.example: The monitorial duties rotated each week.

items.meaningCN: 告诫；温和地责备（ad- 向 + mon- 警告）
items.example: The coach admonished the players for arriving late.
items.exampleCN: 教练因球员迟到而告诫了他们。

items.example: She ignored the admonition and drove faster.
items.exampleCN: 她无视那句告诫，反而开得更快。

items.meaning: a warning, especially an official one
items.meaningCN: 警告；正式告诫（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: The court issued a monition to the landowner.
items.exampleCN: 法院向那位土地所有者发出正式警告。

items.meaning: a feeling that something is coming
items.meaningCN: 预感；事前警告（pre- 在前 + monition 警告）
items.example: She had a premonition that the flight would be delayed.
items.exampleCN: 她预感到那趟航班会延误。

items.meaningCN: 召唤；传唤（sum- 暗中 + mon- 提醒）
items.example: The manager summoned the clerk to her office.
items.exampleCN: 经理把那名职员叫到办公室。

items.structure: Greek Mentor, perhaps from PIE *men- 'to think'
items.meaningCN: 导师；可信赖的顾问（同出“思考”词根）
items.example: She became a mentor to the younger researchers.
items.exampleCN: 她成了年轻研究者的导师。

latinEntries.meaning: one who warns, reminds, or checks
